name: Zendesk
description: Zendesk provides customer support software with ticketing, live chat, and knowledge base features, enabling efficient helpdesk operations and customer engagement

tools.name: Apply Zendesk Macro Preview
tools.description: Preview how a Zendesk macro would affect a ticket without actually applying it. Returns the ticket object as it would appear after the macro is applied, showing any changes to fields, comments, status, or other properties. Use this action to review macro changes before applying them to ensure the outcome is as expected.

inputs.name: macro_id
inputs.about: The ID of the macro to apply.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket to preview the macro on.

tools.name: Autocomplete Problems
tools.description: Autocomplete problems in Zendesk. Use when you need to find problem suggestions based on a partial search text for ticket categorization or troubleshooting.

inputs.name: text
inputs.about: The text to search for in problems. Used to find matching problem suggestions.

tools.name: Autocomplete Users
tools.description: Find Zendesk users using autocomplete by name prefix, phone, or lookup relationship, with optional filters. Name or phone searches cannot be combined with lookup relationship parameters.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name to search for matching users. Returns users whose name starts with the provided value. Cannot be combined with field_id/source.

inputs.name: phone
inputs.about: The phone number to search for matching users. Cannot be combined with field_id/source.

inputs.name: filter
inputs.about: Filter to apply to autocomplete results. Common values: 'assignable', 'requester', or 'dynamic_values' object.

inputs.name: source
inputs.about: The type of the object referenced by field_id. When provided, must be one of the recognized values: 'zen:user', 'zen:organization', 'zen:ticket', or 'zen:custom_object:CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY' (also 'zen:article'/'zen:brand' for lookup fields defined on a custom object) — any other value 400s with "Parame

inputs.name: field_id
inputs.about: Field ID for lookup relationship autocomplete. If source is also provided, it must be a recognized type string — an unrecognized value 400s with "Parameter source must be a valid type is required". field_id alone (with no source) is accepted and simply returns no matches. Cannot be combined with nam

tools.name: Check Host Mapping Validity for Existing Brand
tools.description: Check the host mapping validity for an existing brand in Zendesk. Returns the current CNAME record, expected CNAME values, validity status, and the reason for validity or invalidity. Use this action when you need to verify that DNS records are correctly configured for an existing brand that has already been created in Zendesk. This action requires a brand ID rather than subdomain/host_mapping parameters.

inputs.name: brand_id
inputs.about: The ID of the brand to check host mapping validity for.

tools.name: Count Deleted Users
tools.description: Retrieve the count of deleted users in Zendesk, along with its refresh timestamp. The count value may be null.

tools.name: Count User CCD Tickets
tools.description: Count tickets where the specified user is CCD (carbon copy distribution). Returns an approximate count of tickets where the user appears in the CCD field. Use when you need to know how many tickets a user is copied on for reporting or operational purposes.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk user whose CCD tickets to count. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads (requester_id, submitter_id, assignee_id, author_id).

tools.name: Count Custom Object Records
tools.description: Count the number of records in a specific Zendesk custom object. Use when you need to determine the total number of records for a custom object type, which is useful for reporting, capacity planning, or validation before creating new records. This is a read-only, idempotent operation. Example use cases: - Check if a custom object has records before deleting - Get record count for reporting dashboards - Verify capacity before bulk operations

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

tools.name: Count Zendesk Organizations
tools.description: Count the number of organizations in Zendesk. Returns an approximate count of organizations with the timestamp of when the count was last calculated. This is a read-only, idempotent operation. Use when you need to know the total number of organizations for reporting, capacity planning, or operational purposes. For detailed per-organization information, use ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS instead.

tools.name: Create Access Rule
tools.description: Create an access rule for a custom object in Zendesk. Access rules control which users can view or modify custom object records based on conditions. Use when you need to set up data access policies for custom objects, such as limiting access to records created by the current user or records assigned to specific groups. Returns the created access rule with its ID, title, description, conditions, and timestamps.

inputs.name: access_rule
inputs.about: The access rule definition including title, description, and conditions

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of the custom object to create an access rule for

tools.name: Install Zendesk App
tools.description: Install a Zendesk app in the account. Use when you need to add an app from the Zendesk marketplace or a private app to your Zendesk instance. You must provide the app_id; settings are optional for apps that have defaults or no configurable settings. This action is irreversible once installed.

inputs.name: app_id
inputs.about: The ID of the app to install

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.about: Whether the app should be enabled after installation. When omitted, Zendesk's server-side default applies (currently `true` for most apps). Pass `True` or `False` to override that default explicitly.

inputs.name: settings
inputs.about: Installation settings as a flat key-value object. All apps support the 'name' setting. Example: {'name': 'My App', 'iframeURL': 'https://example.com'}. Use either 'settings' or 'settings_objects', not both.

inputs.name: settings_objects
inputs.about: Alternative format for settings using key-value objects. Use either 'settings' or 'settings_objects', not both.

inputs.name: recurring_payment
inputs.about: Enable recurring Stripe payment subscription for paid apps. Set to true to enable billing.

inputs.name: role_restrictions
inputs.about: List of user roles to restrict the app to. Valid values: 'end-user', 'agent', 'admin'

inputs.name: group_restrictions
inputs.about: List of Zendesk group IDs to restrict the app to. Only users in these groups can see the app.

tools.name: Send Notification to App
tools.description: Send a notification to currently open instances of a Zendesk app. Use when you need to push real-time notifications or data to a Zendesk app that is currently open in an agent's interface. The notification triggers an event in the app, which can then respond with custom behavior (e.g., display a popup, update UI, trigger a workflow). Only works with apps that are currently open in the Zendesk interface.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: The message body or data to send to the app. Can be a string, number, boolean, object, array, or null. Maximum payload size is 1MB.

inputs.name: event
inputs.about: The name of the event that will fire in the app. This is a custom event string that the app listens for to trigger its own logic.

inputs.name: app_id
inputs.about: The ID of the app to send the notification to. Set to 0 for unpublished apps in development mode.

inputs.name: agent_id
inputs.about: The ID of a specific agent to notify. If not provided, the notification will be sent to all currently open instances of the app.

tools.name: Create Article in Section
tools.description: Create a Help Center article in a selected section.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: Article body as HTML.

inputs.name: draft
inputs.about: Whether to create a draft. Publishing requires permission-group rights.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: Article title. Required with locale unless translations are provided.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.about: Enabled Help Center locale. Required with title unless translations are provided.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Article position in the section.

inputs.name: promoted
inputs.about: Whether the article is promoted.

inputs.name: author_id
inputs.about: ID of the article author, as a string.

inputs.name: section_id
inputs.about: Parent Help Center section ID, as a string.

inputs.name: label_names
inputs.about: Label names to assign on supported plans.

inputs.name: translations
inputs.about: Localized article contents. Use instead of top-level title, locale, and body.

inputs.name: content_tag_ids
inputs.about: Existing content tag IDs to attach.

inputs.name: user_segment_id
inputs.about: Single viewer segment ID; omit or set null for a public article.

inputs.name: user_segment_ids
inputs.about: Viewer segment IDs; an empty list makes the article public.

inputs.name: comments_disabled
inputs.about: Whether comments are disabled.

inputs.name: notify_subscribers
inputs.about: Whether subscribers receive the article creation email.

inputs.name: permission_group_id
inputs.about: Permission group allowed to edit and publish, as a string.

tools.name: Create Autocomplete Tags
tools.description: Search for Zendesk tags using autocomplete via POST request body. Use when you need to find tag suggestions based on a partial tag name for tagging tickets or organizing content.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: A substring of a tag name to search for. The API returns registered and recent tags matching this substring.

tools.name: Create Automation
tools.description: Create a new automation in Zendesk. Automations are business rules that automatically perform actions on tickets when certain conditions are met. Automations run server-side and don't require user interaction. Use this action when you need to: - Automatically assign tickets based on conditions - Change ticket priority/status based on rules - Add tags to tickets matching certain criteria - Notify agents or teams based on ticket properties - Implement escalation workflows Note: Automations must have at least one condition that is time-based (like created_at, updated_at) OR check one of: status, type, group_id, assignee_id, or requester_id.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title/name of the automation. Must be unique among all automations.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the automation is active and will execute. Set to false to create a draft automation.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: List of actions the automation will perform when triggered. Each action specifies a field to modify and the value to set.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The position of the automation which specifies the order it will be executed. Lower numbers execute first. If not specified, the automation is added to the end.

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: The conditions that must be met for the automation to execute. At least one 'all' condition must reference a time-based field (created_at, updated_at, etc.) or check: status, type, group_id, assignee_id, or requester_id. Omitting it would post `{"all": [], "any": []}` to Zendesk and fail server-side

tools.name: Create Bookmark
tools.description: Create a bookmark for a ticket in Zendesk. Bookmarks allow you to save references to tickets for quick access. Use this action when you need to: - Save a ticket for later reference - Mark an important ticket for quick access - Create a watchlist-like functionality for specific tickets

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket to bookmark. The ticket must exist and the user must have permission to access it.

tools.name: Redact Zendesk Comment
tools.description: Redact specified text from a Zendesk ticket comment using the Agent Workspace method. Redaction is irreversible; Agent Workspace and appropriate permissions are required, and comments on closed tickets cannot be redacted.

inputs.name: text
inputs.about: The exact text string to redact from the comment. Required: omitting it would send an empty payload to the redact endpoint and report success without any redaction having happened. The text must match exactly as it appears in the comment.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket containing the comment to redact.

inputs.name: ticket_comment_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket comment to redact.

tools.name: Create Custom Object Bulk Job
tools.description: Submit a bulk job to create, update, delete, or upsert Zendesk custom object records. Delete items must be objects containing an id or name; the response may include a job ID for tracking progress.

inputs.name: items
inputs.about: Array of record objects for create, update, or upsert actions. Each object contains the record attributes matching the custom object's field definitions. For delete actions, this should be an array of record IDs (strings).

inputs.name: action
inputs.about: The bulk operation to perform. 'create' adds new records, 'update' modifies existing records, 'delete' removes records, 'upsert' creates or updates based on matching criteria.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of the custom object to operate on. This is the unique identifier for the custom object type (e.g., 'car', 'product', 'order').

tools.name: Create Custom Object Record
tools.description: Create a record for a Zendesk custom object and return its generated ID and available record fields, including timestamps when provided.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: User-defined display name for the object. If autonumbering is selected for the custom object's name field, the name isn't allowed because it's automatically generated. If uniqueness is enabled, the name must be unique.

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: An id you can use to link custom object records to external data

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car')

inputs.name: custom_object_fields
inputs.about: A dictionary of custom field key-value pairs. The available fields are defined in the custom object's field definitions.

tools.name: Create Custom Object Record Attachment
tools.description: Create an attachment for a Zendesk custom object record by uploading a file as multipart form data; the response may include attachment details and malware scan status. Accepts an uploaded file reference or a data or permitted local file URL, but rejects remote file links.

inputs.name: file
inputs.about: The file to upload as an attachment. The file name will be used for the attachment (for example, 'document.pdf' or 'image.jpg').

inputs.name: record_id
inputs.about: The id of a custom object record

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car')

tools.name: Create Custom Ticket Status
tools.description: Create a new custom ticket status in Zendesk. Custom statuses allow agents to define more granular ticket states beyond the default status categories. Use when you need to add custom ticket workflow states to better reflect your support process. Both `agent_label`, `status_category`, `end_user_label`, and `description` are required. The status category determines which lifecycle phase the custom status belongs to.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the custom status is active. Defaults to true. If false, the status is inactive and cannot be selected.

inputs.name: agent_label
inputs.about: The label displayed to agents when this custom status is shown. Maximum length is 48 characters.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: The description explaining when an agent should select this custom ticket status.

inputs.name: end_user_label
inputs.about: The label displayed to end users (customers) when this custom status is shown. Maximum length is 48 characters.

inputs.name: status_category
inputs.about: The status category this custom status belongs to. Must be one of: 'new', 'open', 'pending', 'hold', 'solved'.

inputs.name: end_user_description
inputs.about: The description displayed to end users (customers) about this status.

tools.name: Create Deletion Schedule
tools.description: Create a Zendesk deletion schedule for records matching specified conditions, for retention or cleanup. The schedule is active by default, and its target object type cannot be changed after creation.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title/name of the deletion schedule. Must be descriptive so you can identify it in the Zendesk admin panel.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the deletion schedule is active and will execute. Set to false to create a disabled schedule.

inputs.name: object
inputs.about: The entity type to delete. Cannot be modified after creation. Built-in values: 'zen:ticket' (tickets), 'zen:user' (users), 'zen:attachment' (attachments), 'zen:bot_only_conversation' (bot conversations). For custom objects, use 'zen:custom_object:CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY' (the enum was widened to accept th

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: Conditions object for deletion schedule - defines when items should be deleted.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A description explaining what this deletion schedule does.

tools.name: Create Zendesk Dynamic Content Item
tools.description: Create a new dynamic content item with locale variants in Zendesk. Dynamic content items enable localized content for ticket fields, macros, and other text-based content. Use when setting up multilingual support or creating template content that varies by user locale. The item's name cannot be changed after creation. Ensure the name is descriptive and follows your naming conventions.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Unique name for the dynamic content item. This name is used to reference the item in macros, triggers, and other content. Must be unique within the account.

inputs.name: variants
inputs.about: Array of locale variants for this item. At least one variant is required. Each variant provides content for a specific locale.

inputs.name: default_locale_id
inputs.about: The ID of the default locale for this item. Must be one of the locales the account has active.

tools.name: Create Zendesk Dynamic Content Item Variant
tools.description: Create a new locale variant for an existing dynamic content item in Zendesk. Use when you need to add support for a new locale to an existing dynamic content item. Note: You can only create one variant per locale per dynamic content item. Use the update action to modify existing variants.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: If true, the variant is active and usable. Set to false to create a draft variant.

inputs.name: content
inputs.about: The content text for this locale variant. This is the localized string that will be displayed.

inputs.name: default
inputs.about: If true, this is the default variant used when no matching locale is found. Only one variant should be marked as default per item.

inputs.name: locale_id
inputs.about: The ID of the locale for this variant. Must be one of the locales the account has active.

inputs.name: dynamic_content_item_id
inputs.about: The ID of the dynamic content item to add a variant to

tools.name: Create End User Identity
tools.description: Add an identity (email or phone) to an end user's profile in Zendesk. Use when you need to link a new email address or phone number to an existing end user account.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The type of identity to create. Must be one of: 'email', 'phone_number', 'twitter', 'facebook', 'google', 'agent_forwarding', 'any_channel', 'foreign', 'sdk', 'messaging'.

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The identifier value (e.g., email address like 'user@example.com' or phone number in E.164 format)

inputs.name: primary
inputs.about: If true, marks this identity as the primary identity for the user. Writable only at creation time.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the end user to add the identity to

tools.name: Create Zendesk Group Membership
tools.description: Create a group membership in Zendesk, assigning an agent to a group. Use when you need to add an agent to a specific group for ticket routing, permissions, or team organization. The user_id and group_id are both required parameters. Note: The user must exist and have appropriate permissions to be assigned to groups. The group must also exist.

inputs.name: default
inputs.about: If true, tickets assigned directly to the agent will assume this membership's group. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the agent to assign to the group. You can find this from user search results or ticket payloads (requester_id, submitter_id, assignee_id, author_id).

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the group to assign the agent to. You can find this from group list results or ticket group_id fields.

tools.name: Bulk Import Tickets
tools.description: Bulk import tickets into Zendesk by posting up to 100 ticket objects at a time. Use when migrating tickets from another system or creating multiple tickets in a single API call. The operation returns a job_status payload; the initial status is typically 'queued' or 'completed' for small batches. This action is useful for data migration, test data setup, and bulk ticket creation workflows.

inputs.name: tickets
inputs.about: Array of up to 100 ticket objects to import. Each ticket can have any valid ticket field.

inputs.name: archive_immediately
inputs.about: If true, any ticket created with a 'closed' status bypasses the normal ticket lifecycle and will be created directly in your ticket archive

tools.name: Create Macro
tools.description: Create a Zendesk macro that agents can apply to tickets.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the macro.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the macro is displayed in Zendesk.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: One or more actions the macro performs when applied.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The position of the macro in the macro list.

inputs.name: attachments
inputs.about: Macro attachment IDs to associate with the macro.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A description of what the macro does.

inputs.name: restriction
inputs.about: The users or groups that may access the macro.

tools.name: Create Many Dynamic Content Variants
tools.description: Create multiple locale variants for an existing Zendesk dynamic content item in one request, supplying localized content and active status. The default-variant flag is not sent.

inputs.name: variants
inputs.about: Array of locale variants to create. Each variant provides content for a specific locale.

inputs.name: dynamic_content_item_id
inputs.about: The ID of the dynamic content item to add variants to.

tools.name: Create Many Zendesk Tickets
tools.description: Create many tickets in Zendesk in a single request. Accepts an array of up to 100 ticket objects. The operation is handled asynchronously — a background job is queued and you receive a job_status payload with an initial status of 'queued' or 'working'. Poll the job_status URL or use ZENDESK_GET_APPS_JOB_STATUS to check for completion and view per-ticket results. Use when creating multiple tickets at once or seeding test data. This action is irreversible — tickets created cannot be easily undone once the job completes. Ensure the tickets list is accurate before submitting.

inputs.name: tickets
inputs.about: Array of ticket objects to create (max 100). Each ticket requires at minimum a 'subject' field.

tools.name: Create Many Zendesk Users
tools.description: Create many users in Zendesk in a single request. Accepts up to 100 user objects. The operation is handled asynchronously — a background job is queued and you receive a job_status payload with an initial status of 'queued' or 'working'. Poll the job_status URL or use ZENDESK_GET_APPS_JOB_STATUS to check for completion and view per-user results. Use when onboarding multiple users at once or seeding test data. Note: This action is idempotent — re-running with the same external_ids may update existing users depending on Zendesk configuration.

inputs.name: users
inputs.about: Array of user objects to create (max 100). Each user requires a 'name' field.

inputs.name: skip_verify_email
inputs.about: If true, do not send verification emails to new users. Passed as a URL query parameter.

tools.name: Create Object Trigger
tools.description: Create a trigger for a Zendesk custom object, defining conditions and actions for automated workflows on its records.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title/name of the trigger. Must be unique within the custom object.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the trigger is active and will execute. Set to false to create a draft trigger.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: List of actions the trigger will perform when conditions are met. Each action specifies a field and value.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The position of the trigger which specifies the order it will be executed. Lower numbers execute first.

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: The conditions that must be met for the trigger to execute. Conditions use 'all' (AND) and 'any' (OR) logic.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A description of what the trigger does.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of the custom object to create a trigger for. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

tools.name: Create Organization Field
tools.description: Create a custom organization field in Zendesk. Use when you need to add a new custom field type (such as text, dropdown, checkbox, date, etc.) to track additional organization attributes. The field key must be unique and can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores.

inputs.name: key
inputs.about: A unique key that identifies this custom field. Must consist of only letters, numbers, and underscores. Cannot be only numbers.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.about: Optional tag for checkbox type fields

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The custom field type. Must be one of: checkbox, date, decimal, dropdown, integer, lookup, multiselect, regexp, text, or textarea

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the custom field

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: If true, this field is available for use. Defaults to true.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Ordering of the field relative to other fields. Lower values appear first.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: User-defined description of the field's purpose

inputs.name: relationship_filter
inputs.about: Filter definition for autocomplete in lookup fields

inputs.name: custom_field_options
inputs.about: Required for dropdown or multiselect types. Each option requires a name and value.

inputs.name: regexp_for_validation
inputs.about: Regular expression pattern for validating regexp type fields

inputs.name: relationship_target_type
inputs.about: Object type referenced for lookup fields. Can be zen:user, zen:organization, zen:ticket, or zen:custom_object:{key}

tools.name: Create Organization Membership
tools.description: Create an organization membership in Zendesk by assigning a user to an organization. By default, the request marks the membership as the user's default organization; this can be changed.

inputs.name: default
inputs.about: Denotes whether this is the default organization membership for the user. If set to true, this membership will be the primary organization for the user. Defaults to true if not specified.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user to assign to the organization. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_LIST_USERS or ZENDESK_SEARCH_USERS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: The ID of the organization to assign the user to. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS or ZENDESK_GET_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATION_BY_ID; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

tools.name: Create Many Organization Memberships
tools.description: Create multiple organization memberships in Zendesk by posting up to 100 membership objects at a time. Each membership links a user to an organization. Use when onboarding multiple users to organizations in bulk, such as during team migrations or organizational restructuring. The operation returns a job_status payload; the initial status is typically 'queued' for larger batches.

inputs.name: organization_memberships
inputs.about: Array of organization membership objects to create (max 100). Each object requires user_id and organization_id.

tools.name: Merge Zendesk Organizations
tools.description: Merge two Zendesk organizations by combining all users, tickets, and data from the losing organization into the winning organization. This action is irreversible — once merged, the losing organization and all its data cannot be recovered. Use when you need to consolidate duplicate organizations or combine organization data into a single organization.

inputs.name: winner_id
inputs.about: The ID of the winning organization that will receive all users and tickets from the losing organization

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: The ID of the organization to merge from (the losing organization that will be merged into another)

tools.name: Set Organization Tags
tools.description: Set organization tags in Zendesk by making a POST request to replace the tags on an organization. Use when you need to categorize or label organizations with specific tags for filtering and organization purposes. This operation replaces all existing tags on the organization with the new set provided. Note: This action is not idempotent as it replaces existing tags rather than adding to them.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: An array of tag strings to set for the organization. Tags are used to categorize and filter organizations. Existing tags on the organization will be replaced with this new set of tags.

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: The ID of the organization to set tags for. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS or ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

tools.name: Create Organization Subscription
tools.description: Create an organization subscription in Zendesk. This subscribes a user to receive notifications and updates related to a specific organization. Use when you need to add a user to an organization's subscription list so they can access organization-related resources and receive notifications.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user who will be subscribed to the organization

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: The ID of the organization to subscribe the user to

tools.name: Create Or Update Many Users
tools.description: Create or update up to 100 Zendesk users in a single request; new users require a name. Returns a background job status, with per-user results when available.

inputs.name: users
inputs.about: Array of user objects to create or update. Up to 100 users can be included. For new users, 'name' is required. For existing users, 'id' is required to identify the user to update.

tools.name: Create Or Update Organization
tools.description: Create or update a Zendesk organization in a single operation. If an organization with the same external_id already exists, it is updated. Otherwise, a new organization is created. Use when you need to ensure an organization exists without checking for duplicates first. Note: For updates, you must specify the external_id to match the existing organization. Name is not available as a matching criteria.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: A unique name for the organization. Required when creating a new organization. Note: Name is not available as a matching criteria for updates - use external_id or id instead.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: The tags of the organization

inputs.name: notes
inputs.about: Any notes you have about the organization

inputs.name: details
inputs.about: Any details about the organization, such as the address

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: New tickets from users in this organization are automatically put in this group

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: A unique external id to associate organizations to an external record. The id is case-insensitive (e.g., 'company1' and 'Company1' are considered the same). Use this for matching when updating an existing organization.

inputs.name: domain_names
inputs.about: An array of domain names associated with this organization

inputs.name: shared_tickets
inputs.about: End users in this organization are able to see each other's tickets

inputs.name: shared_comments
inputs.about: End users in this organization are able to comment on each other's tickets

inputs.name: organization_fields
inputs.about: Custom fields for this organization. See custom organization fields documentation for available field definitions.

tools.name: Create or Update User
tools.description: Create or update a Zendesk user, matching existing users by email or external_id. Returns the user object.

inputs.name: user
inputs.about: User object with attributes. `name` is mandatory. The user is matched by `email` or `external_id` to determine create vs update. `role` must be one of: 'end-user', 'agent', or 'admin'.

tools.name: Bulk Unregister Push Notification Devices
tools.description: Bulk unregister push notification devices in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the devices will be permanently removed from receiving push notifications and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete device tokens or removing test devices from receiving push notifications.

inputs.name: push_notification_devices
inputs.about: List of mobile device tokens to unregister from push notifications. These are the device tokens returned when a mobile device registers for push notifications.

tools.name: Create Resource Collection
tools.description: Create a resource collection in Zendesk. Use when you need to batch multiple operations on Zendesk resources (like tickets) into a single request. The API processes the collection as a background job and returns a job status object. Note: This action queues a background job. Poll the returned job_status.url to check when the collection has been processed.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title/name of the resource collection. This is used to identify the collection.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: Array of action objects specifying what to do with the resources. Each action has a type and list of resource IDs.

tools.name: Create Side Conversation
tools.description: Create a private side conversation on a Zendesk ticket. Side conversations are agent-to-agent communications that don't notify the customer. Use this action when you need to discuss a ticket privately with another agent, escalate to a specialist, or coordinate on sensitive issues without customer visibility. Recipients can include Zendesk users (by ID or email), Slack channels, support groups, or Microsoft Teams channels.

inputs.name: to
inputs.about: List of recipients for the side conversation. Each recipient must have at least one of: user_id, email, slack_channel_id, support_group_id, or msteams_channel_id. At least one recipient is required.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: Plain text body of the initial message. This is the main content of the side conversation that recipients will see.

inputs.name: subject
inputs.about: Subject line for the side conversation. If not provided, a default subject may be used based on the parent ticket.

inputs.name: html_body
inputs.about: HTML-formatted body of the initial message. If provided, this will be used instead of the plain text body for HTML-capable clients.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: The ID of the Zendesk ticket to attach the side conversation to

inputs.name: external_ids
inputs.about: Key-value external metadata to attach to the side conversation. Use this to store custom identifiers or tags from your external systems.

inputs.name: attachment_ids
inputs.about: List of attachment file IDs to include with the message. These must be IDs from previously uploaded attachments via the CreateSideConversationAttachment action.

tools.name: Create Support Address
tools.description: Create a new support address (recipient address) in Zendesk. Use when you need to add a new email address for receiving support requests. The email address must follow Zendesk's format (`{local-part}@{accountname}.zendesk.com`) for internal addresses, or be an existing external email with forwarding properly configured. The created address will have verification statuses that indicate whether DNS records (CNAME, SPF) are properly configured. Note that you cannot change the email address of an existing support address after creation.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name for the address

inputs.name: email
inputs.about: The email address for the support address. Note: You cannot change the email address of an existing support address after creation.

inputs.name: default
inputs.about: Whether this address should be the account's default support address

inputs.name: brand_id
inputs.about: The ID of the brand to associate with this support address. If not provided, the address will be associated with the account's default brand.

tools.name: Export Suspended Tickets
tools.description: Export Suspended Tickets from Zendesk Support. Use when you need to export all suspended tickets for compliance review, audit purposes, or data analysis. This action enqueues a job that creates a CSV file; when complete, Zendesk emails the requester a link to download the CSV. Suspended tickets are sorted by update timestamp in ascending order. Rate limited to one request per minute. Note: This action is read-only and returns the export job status. The actual CSV will be sent via email when the job completes.

tools.name: Create Ticket Content Pin
tools.description: Create a ticket content pin in Zendesk. Content pins allow you to attach helpful resources like Help Center articles or external content directly to tickets for easy reference. Use this action when you need to: - Attach a Help Center article to a ticket for context - Pin an external knowledge base article to a ticket - Add relevant documentation or resources to a support ticket

inputs.name: locale
inputs.about: The locale for the content pin. Required when content_type is 'external_content' — Zendesk rejects external-content pins with no locale ('External contents must have locale to be able to get pinned to tickets.'). Also required when pinning articles. Format: language + underscore + locale code (e.g.,

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket to which the content pin will be added

inputs.name: content_id
inputs.about: The ID of the content to pin

inputs.name: content_type
inputs.about: The type of content being pinned. Common values include 'article' for Help Center articles and 'external_content' for external resources.

tools.name: Create Ticket Field
tools.description: Create a custom ticket field in Zendesk with various field types. Use when you need to add a new custom field (such as text, dropdown, checkbox, date, numeric, regex-validated, or lookup) to capture additional information on tickets. The field title is required; description, required flag, and custom options are optional.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.about: For checkbox fields only. The tag added to tickets when the checkbox is selected

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The ticket field type. Must be one of: text, textarea, checkbox, date, integer, decimal, regexp, partialcreditcard, multiselect, tagger, or lookup

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the ticket field shown to agents and end users

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: If true, this field is available for use. Defaults to true.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Relative position of the field on the ticket. Fields with lower positions appear first.

inputs.name: required
inputs.about: If true, agents must enter a value in this field to change the ticket status to solved. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: User-defined description explaining the purpose of this field

inputs.name: agent_can_edit
inputs.about: If true, agents can edit this field. Defaults to true.

inputs.name: title_in_portal
inputs.about: The title shown to end users in Help Center (may differ from agent title)

inputs.name: agent_description
inputs.about: A description of the ticket field that only agents can see

inputs.name: visible_in_portal
inputs.about: If true, the field is visible to end users in Help Center. Defaults to true.

inputs.name: editable_in_portal
inputs.about: If true, end users can edit this field in Help Center. Defaults to true.

inputs.name: required_in_portal
inputs.about: If true, end users must enter a value to create a request. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: relationship_filter
inputs.about: Filter definition that allows autocomplete to filter down results for lookup fields

inputs.name: collapsed_for_agents
inputs.about: If true, the field is hidden alongside infrequently used fields. Classic interface only.

inputs.name: custom_field_options
inputs.about: Required for multiselect and tagger types. Defines the available options for dropdown selection.

inputs.name: regexp_for_validation
inputs.about: Regular expression pattern for validating input on regexp type fields

inputs.name: relationship_target_type
inputs.about: The type of object referenced by lookup fields. Can be zen:user, zen:organization, zen:ticket, or zen:custom_object:{key}

tools.name: Create Ticket Field Option
tools.description: Create or update an option for a dropdown or multiselect ticket field. Use when you need to add a new selectable option to a custom ticket field of type 'multiselect' or 'tagger'. If an option with the same value already exists, it will be updated with the provided name. This action is idempotent - running it multiple times with the same value will update the existing option rather than creating duplicates.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the option displayed to agents and end users in the dropdown

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The internal value of the option used when saving the ticket field selection

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The relative position of the option in the dropdown list. Options with lower positions appear first.

inputs.name: allow_solving
inputs.about: If true, selecting this option allows the ticket to be solved when the field is required to solve

inputs.name: ticket_field_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket field to add the option to. The ticket field must be of type 'multiselect' or 'tagger'.

tools.name: Create Trigger
tools.description: Create a new trigger in Zendesk. Triggers are business rules that automatically perform actions on tickets when certain conditions are met. Unlike automations, triggers execute immediately when tickets are created or updated. Use this action when you need to: - Automatically change ticket status based on conditions - Assign tickets to agents or groups based on rules - Add tags to tickets matching certain criteria - Send notifications to agents, groups, or external systems - Update custom fields based on ticket properties Note: Triggers must have at least one condition in the 'all' array that references a time-based field (like created_at, updated_at) OR checks one of: status, type, group_id, assignee_id, requester_id, custom_status_id.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title/name of the trigger. Must be unique among all triggers.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the trigger is active and will execute. Set to false to create a draft trigger.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: List of actions the trigger will perform when triggered. Each action specifies a field to modify and the value to set.

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: The conditions that must be met for the trigger to execute. At least one 'all' condition must reference a time-based field (created_at, updated_at) or check: status, type, group_id, assignee_id, requester_id, custom_status_id.

inputs.name: category_id
inputs.about: The ID of the category to assign the trigger to. Categories help organize triggers in the Zendesk admin interface.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A description of what the trigger does.

tools.name: Create Trigger Categories Batch Job
tools.description: Submit a batch patch job for Zendesk ticket trigger categories by ID. The response can include status, results, and errors.

inputs.name: action
inputs.about: The batch action to perform on trigger categories. Currently only 'patch' is supported.

inputs.name: trigger_category_ids
inputs.about: List of trigger category IDs to include in the batch job

tools.name: Create Zendesk Trigger Category
tools.description: Create a new trigger category in Zendesk. Trigger categories are used to organize and group triggers for better management. Use when setting up automated workflows or organizing business rules. This action creates a trigger category with the specified name and optional position. The name must be unique within the account.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the trigger category. Names must be unique within the account.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The position of the trigger category. Triggers with lower positions are run first.

tools.name: Create User Field Option
tools.description: Create or update an option for a dropdown or multiselect user field. Use when you need to add a new selectable option to a custom user field of type 'multiselect' or 'tagger'. If an option with the same value already exists, it will be updated with the provided name. This action is idempotent - running it multiple times with the same value will update the existing option rather than creating duplicates.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the option displayed to agents and end users in the dropdown

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The internal value of the option used when saving the user field selection

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The relative position of the option in the dropdown list. Options with lower positions appear first.

inputs.name: allow_solving
inputs.about: If true, selecting this option allows the ticket to be solved when the field is required to solve

inputs.name: user_field_id
inputs.about: The ID or key of the user field to add the option to. The user field must be of type 'multiselect' or 'tagger'.

tools.name: Create User Identity
tools.description: Tool to add an identity to a user's profile in Zendesk. An agent can add multiple identities to a user (e.g., multiple email addresses). Use this when a user needs to be contacted via a new channel or needs an additional identifier. Use when you need to add an additional identity (email, phone, social) to an existing Zendesk user.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The type of identity to create. Common types include 'email', 'twitter', 'phone_number', etc.

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The identifier value for this identity, such as an email address, phone number, or social media handle.

inputs.name: primary
inputs.about: Set to true to make this identity the primary identity for the user. Defaults to false. Note: Primary can only be set on creation, not on update.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user to add the identity to. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads (requester_id, submitter_id, assignee_id, author_id) or from user search results.

tools.name: Create User Profile Event
tools.description: Store an event against a Sunshine user profile identified by the supplied identifiers, creating the profile if it does not exist. Event properties are limited to name and description.

inputs.name: event
inputs.about: Event information containing the event details and properties.

inputs.name: profile
inputs.about: Profile information for the user who triggered the event. The profile is created if it doesn't exist.

tools.name: Logout Many Zendesk Users
tools.description: Log out multiple users in Zendesk by ending their active sessions. This action is irreversible — the affected users will be logged out and will need to re-authenticate. Use when you need to immediately terminate sessions for multiple users (e.g., after security incident, offboarding, or credential revocation). The operation accepts up to 100 user IDs at a time.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of up to 100 user IDs to log out. The IDs must belong to end-users or agents, not brands or organizations.

tools.name: Create User Organization Membership
tools.description: Create a new organization membership for a specific user in Zendesk by assigning a user to an organization. Use when you need to associate an existing user with an organization so they can access organization-specific tickets and data. This action targets a specific user by their ID. This action is idempotent in that creating a duplicate membership will fail with a specific error, but the operation itself is not naturally idempotent.

inputs.name: default
inputs.about: Denotes whether this is the default organization membership for the user. If set to true, this membership will be the primary organization for the user. Defaults to false if not specified.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user for whom to create the organization membership. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_LIST_USERS or ZENDESK_SEARCH_USERS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: The ID of the organization to assign the user to. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS or ZENDESK_GET_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATION_BY_ID; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

tools.name: Create Users Tags
tools.description: Set tags on a Zendesk user via POST request to /api/v2/users/{user_id}/tags. Use when you need to add or update tags on a specific user. Note that this replaces all existing tags on the user with the provided set of tags. This action is idempotent.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: An array of tag names to set on the user. Existing tags will be replaced with these tags.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user to set tags for

tools.name: Create View
tools.description: Create a new view in Zendesk. Views are saved ticket filters that help agents organize and prioritize their work. They can filter tickets by conditions like status, priority, assignee, and more. Use this action when you need to: - Create a custom view for a specific team or workflow - Set up views for different ticket priorities or statuses - Create views with restricted access for specific groups - Configure views with specific columns, grouping, and sort order Note: At minimum, the 'all' conditions must include a condition checking 'status', 'type', 'group_id', 'assignee_id', or 'requester_id'.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the view. Must be unique within the account.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the view is active and visible to agents. Set to false to save as a draft.

inputs.name: output
inputs.about: Output configuration for view display settings.

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: The conditions that define which tickets appear in the view. 'all' conditions must ALL be true; 'any' conditions allow OR logic. At least one 'all' condition is required.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: The description of the view shown to agents.

inputs.name: restriction
inputs.about: Restriction settings for view access.

tools.name: Preview View
tools.description: Preview a Zendesk view by constructing conditions and execution settings to see which tickets match. Use when you need to test or validate view conditions before saving, or to retrieve a live preview of tickets matching specific filter criteria without creating a permanent view. This action is useful for verifying view logic, testing conditions, and previewing results before committing to a saved view.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number). Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.

inputs.name: view
inputs.about: The view object containing title, conditions, and execution settings to preview

inputs.name: columns
inputs.about: Optional list of column definitions to override or extend the view's columns in the output

inputs.name: exclude
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of sideloads to exclude from the response.

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of sideloads to include in the response.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page. Default and maximum values vary by endpoint.

tools.name: Preview View Ticket Count
tools.description: Preview ticket count for a view in Zendesk. Returns the number of tickets matching the specified conditions before saving the view. Use when you want to verify how many tickets will match a view's filter criteria before creating or updating a view. This action sends a POST request to /api/v2/views/preview/count with view conditions and returns the matching ticket count. Rate limited to 5 requests per minute, per view, per agent.

inputs.name: output
inputs.about: Output configuration for view sorting and grouping.

inputs.name: all_conditions
inputs.about: Array of one or more conditions that a ticket must meet ALL of to be included. This is the 'all' array in the view object. At least one condition is required. Note: 'all' is a Python keyword, so this field is named 'all_conditions' but maps to 'all' in the API.

inputs.name: any_conditions
inputs.about: Array of conditions where a ticket meets ANY of them to be included. Optional - if not provided, only 'all_conditions' are used. Note: 'any' is a Python keyword, so this field is named 'any_conditions' but maps to 'any' in the API.

tools.name: Create Webhook
tools.description: Create a standard outbound webhook in Zendesk.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name of the webhook.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Whether the webhook is active or inactive.

inputs.name: endpoint
inputs.about: Absolute HTTPS destination URL that Zendesk notifies.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Description of the webhook.

inputs.name: http_method
inputs.about: HTTP method Zendesk uses for requests to the destination.

inputs.name: subscriptions
inputs.about: One or more Zendesk event types that trigger the webhook. Use only conditional_ticket_events for a trigger or automation webhook; native Zendesk event subscriptions require http_method POST and request_format json.

inputs.name: authentication
inputs.about: Optional destination authentication. Select one type and provide its required data; Zendesk adds it to request headers.

inputs.name: custom_headers
inputs.about: Non-credential headers Zendesk sends to the destination.

inputs.name: request_format
inputs.about: Format of the data Zendesk sends to the destination.

tools.name: Upload Zendesk Attachment
tools.description: Upload a file attachment to Zendesk for use in a ticket comment, returning attachment details and an upload token valid for 60 minutes. Use an uploaded file reference, data URL, or permitted local file URL.

inputs.name: file
inputs.about: The file to upload to Zendesk. The file name will be used for the attachment (for example, 'document.pdf' or 'error_log.txt').

tools.name: Create Zendesk Custom Object
tools.description: Create a new custom object in Zendesk. Use when you need to define a new custom object type to store and manage custom data. The key is immutable once created, so choose carefully.

inputs.name: custom_object
inputs.about: The custom object definition containing key, title, title_pluralized, and optional properties.

tools.name: Create Zendesk Custom Object Field
tools.description: Create a new field for a custom object in Zendesk. Use when you need to add a new attribute or data field to an existing custom object type. The key is immutable once created. This action is idempotent for the same key, but the key parameter must be unique per custom object.

inputs.name: key
inputs.about: A user-defined unique identifier for the field. Once created, this value cannot be changed.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.about: A tag associated with this field for filtering and organization

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The data type of the field. Common types include: 'text', 'integer', 'boolean', 'float', 'date', 'datetime', 'tag', 'enumeration', 'relation'

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: Display name for the field shown in the Zendesk interface

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the field is active and available for use

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Position of the field in the field list. Lower values appear first.

inputs.name: required
inputs.about: Whether this field is required when creating records. Omit (None) to use Zendesk's server-side default; pass True/False to set explicitly.

inputs.name: properties
inputs.about: Additional properties for a custom object field.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A description of the field to help agents understand its purpose

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of the custom object to add the field to

inputs.name: custom_field_options
inputs.about: List of options for dropdown/enumeration type fields

inputs.name: regexp_for_validation
inputs.about: A regular expression pattern to validate the field value against

inputs.name: relationship_target_type
inputs.about: For relationship fields, the key of the target custom object type

tools.name: Create Zendesk Group
tools.description: Create a Zendesk group with an account-unique name to organize agents for ticket assignment and routing. Returns the group's assigned ID and supported group fields.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the group. Must be unique within the account. Leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed.

inputs.name: is_public
inputs.about: If true, the group is public and visible to all agents. If false, the group is private. Note: You cannot change a private group to a public group after creation.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: An optional description of the group explaining its purpose or responsibilities

tools.name: Import Zendesk Ticket
tools.description: Import a ticket into Zendesk with historical timestamps. This action creates tickets with past `created_at`, `updated_at`, or `solved_at` values, useful for migrating historical data. For real-time ticket creation, use ZENDESK_CREATE_ZENDESK_TICKET. Tickets created with 'closed' status and archive_immediately=true bypass normal lifecycle and go directly to archive.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: Array of tags to apply to the ticket.

inputs.name: due_at
inputs.about: Due date for the ticket in ISO 8601 format. Only applicable for task tickets.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: The state of the ticket. Allowed values: 'new', 'open', 'pending', 'hold', 'solved', 'closed'.

inputs.name: subject
inputs.about: Short summary of the issue for the imported ticket.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: The ID of the group to assign the ticket to.

inputs.name: priority
inputs.about: Zendesk priority. Must be one of: 'urgent', 'high', 'normal', 'low'. Defaults to 'normal'.

inputs.name: email_ccs
inputs.about: Array of email CC objects for adding/removing email CCs.

inputs.name: followers
inputs.about: Array of follower objects for adding/removing followers.

inputs.name: solved_at
inputs.about: The time the ticket was solved (for historical imports) in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: created_at
inputs.about: The time the ticket was created (for historical imports) in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: updated_at
inputs.about: The time the ticket was last updated (for historical imports) in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: assignee_id
inputs.about: The ID of the agent to assign to the ticket.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Long-form description / steps to reproduce. This becomes the initial comment on the ticket.

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: An external ID to link this ticket to records in another system.

inputs.name: ticket_type
inputs.about: The type of this ticket. Allowed values: 'problem', 'incident', 'question', 'task'.

inputs.name: requester_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user who requested this ticket.

inputs.name: collaborators
inputs.about: Array of collaborators to CC on the ticket. Each element can be: a user ID (integer), an email address (string), or an object with 'email' and optional 'name'.

inputs.name: custom_fields
inputs.about: Array of custom field objects with 'id' and 'value' properties.

inputs.name: collaborator_ids
inputs.about: Array of user IDs to add as collaborators (CCs) on the ticket.

inputs.name: custom_status_id
inputs.about: The custom ticket status id of the ticket.

inputs.name: archive_immediately
inputs.about: If true, any ticket created with a 'closed' status bypasses the normal ticket lifecycle and will be created directly in your ticket archive.

tools.name: Create Zendesk Organization
tools.description: Create a new organization in Zendesk. After creation, the organization ID is auto-assigned and returned. Verify the exact ID before performing downstream operations that target this organization. Multiple organizations may share similar names — always confirm the correct organization by ID. This action is irreversible — the organization cannot be recovered once deleted. Use this action when you need to register a new company, customer, or group as a Zendesk organization so you can assign users, tickets, or other resources to it.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: A unique name for the organization. Leading and trailing whitespace are automatically trimmed. Names differing only by whitespace are treated as duplicates.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: The tags of the organization

inputs.name: notes
inputs.about: Any notes you have about the organization

inputs.name: details
inputs.about: Any details about the organization, such as the address

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: New tickets from users in this organization are automatically put in this group

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: A unique external id to associate organizations to an external record

inputs.name: domain_names
inputs.about: An array of domain names associated with this organization

inputs.name: shared_tickets
inputs.about: End users in this organization are able to see each other's tickets

inputs.name: shared_comments
inputs.about: End users in this organization are able to comment on each other's tickets

tools.name: Create Zendesk Request
tools.description: Create a new request in Zendesk. Use when an end user needs to submit a support request through the API. The request will be created with the provided subject, description, priority, and other optional fields. Returns the created request with its ID and URL.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: Array of tags to apply to the request.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The type of the request. Must be one of: 'question', 'incident', 'problem', 'task'.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: The state of the request. Must be one of: 'new', 'open', 'pending', 'hold', 'solved', 'closed'. Defaults to 'new'.

inputs.name: subject
inputs.about: The subject/title of the request. This is a required field.

inputs.name: priority
inputs.about: The priority of the request. Must be one of: 'low', 'normal', 'high', 'urgent'. Defaults to 'normal'.

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: An external ID to link this request to records in another system.

inputs.name: comment_body
inputs.about: The initial description or comment on the request. Required -- Zendesk's Create Request API documents `comment` as mandatory (confirmed live: omitting it returns a 422).

inputs.name: requester_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user making the request.

inputs.name: custom_fields
inputs.about: Custom fields for the request. Each item should include 'id' and 'value' properties.

inputs.name: requester_name
inputs.about: Name of the requester. If provided with requester_email, creates a user object for the requester.

inputs.name: ticket_form_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the ticket form associated with the request. Only applicable for enterprise accounts.

inputs.name: requester_email
inputs.about: Email of the requester. Must be provided together with requester_name.

tools.name: Create Zendesk Target
tools.description: Create a target in Zendesk for triggering outbound integrations. Use when you need to set up a notification channel or integration with external services like Campfire, email, URL webhooks, or other supported targets. Targets can be used with triggers and automation rules. Note: URL targets are being discontinued October 28, 2024 in favor of webhooks. Email targets remain unaffected.

inputs.name: to
inputs.about: Recipient phone number for clickatell targets.

inputs.name: room
inputs.about: Room name or ID for campfire targets.

inputs.name: email
inputs.about: Email address for email targets (recipient) and get_satisfaction targets (auth).

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: A name for the target. Must be unique within the account.

inputs.name: token

inputs.name: dynamic_content_item_id
inputs.about: The ID of the dynamic content item containing the variant to delete

inputs.name: dynamic_content_variant_id
inputs.about: The ID of the variant to delete

tools.name: Delete Zendesk Custom Object Trigger
tools.description: Permanently deletes a custom object trigger in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a specific trigger from a custom object definition. This action is irreversible — the trigger and all its data will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Requires admin permissions.

inputs.name: trigger_id
inputs.about: The ID of the trigger to delete

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of the custom object that contains the trigger to delete

tools.name: Delete Zendesk Organization

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: ID of the organization to delete

tools.name: Delete Zendesk Support Address
tools.description: Permanently deletes a support address from Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the support address cannot be recovered once deleted. Use this action when you need to remove a deprecated or unwanted support email address from your Zendesk account. This operation requires admin permissions and the support address must not be set as the default address. Deleting an address that is actively used may impact email routing.

inputs.name: support_address_id
inputs.about: The ID of the support address to delete

tools.name: Delete Zendesk Ticket
tools.description: Permanently deletes a ticket in Zendesk, including its entire conversation history. This action is irreversible; always confirm the correct ticket_id before executing.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: ID of the ticket to delete

tools.name: Delete Zendesk User
tools.description: Tool to permanently delete a user from Zendesk. Use when you need to remove a user account. This action cannot be undone and requires appropriate admin permissions.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user to delete

tools.name: Bulk Delete Soft-Deleted Zendesk Tickets
tools.description: Permanently deletes multiple soft-deleted tickets in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the tickets will be permanently removed and cannot be recovered once executed. Use when cleaning up test tickets or removing obsolete soft-deleted tickets in bulk. The operation returns a job_status payload (initial status typically 'queued'); deletions complete asynchronously and may require follow-up polling to confirm completion. Maximum 100 tickets per request.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of ticket IDs to permanently delete (max 100). Only soft-deleted tickets can be destroyed.

tools.name: Bulk Delete Zendesk Organizations
tools.description: Bulk delete Zendesk organizations. This action is irreversible - once organizations are deleted, they cannot be recovered. Use when you need to remove multiple organizations in a single operation. Returns a job_status payload (initial status typically 'queued'); deletions complete asynchronously and may require follow-up polling to confirm completion. Maximum 100 organizations per request. Use this action when you need to clean up test data, remove obsolete organizations, or perform bulk organization deletions. You must provide either 'ids' (comma-separated list of Zendesk organization IDs) or 'external_ids' (comma-separated list of external IDs).

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of Zendesk organization IDs to delete (max 100). Required if external_ids is not provided.

inputs.name: external_ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of Zendesk external organization IDs to delete (max 100). Required if ids is not provided.

tools.name: Detect Best Locale
tools.description: Detect a Zendesk locale using the detect-best-locale endpoint and return its locale details. The request uses connection headers rather than accepting browser language settings as an input.

tools.name: Download Attachment
tools.description: Download the file bytes for one Zendesk ticket attachment ID. Zendesk attachment IDs first resolve to metadata. This action then downloads the provider-issued content URL and returns the file for use by other tools.

inputs.name: attachment_id
inputs.about: The attachment ID from a Zendesk ticket comment, as a string.

tools.name: Download Custom Object Record Attachment
tools.description: Download an attachment from a Zendesk custom object record and return it as a downloadable file. An inline option is sent to Zendesk with the request.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The id of a custom object record attachment. You can find attachment IDs in the custom object record's attachment list.

inputs.name: inline
inputs.about: If true, the attachment content is displayed inline in the browser (e.g., for viewing images). If false or omitted, the attachment is downloaded as a file.

inputs.name: record_id
inputs.about: The id of a custom object record. You can find record IDs by listing or searching custom object records.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object. You can find custom object keys by listing custom objects.

tools.name: Get Zendesk About Me
tools.description: Get information about the currently authenticated user in Zendesk. Returns only the caller's own account; to look up other users, use ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK_USERS. Response nests the user object under data.owner_info.user. Useful for verifying the acting user's identity and permissions before performing bulk operations.

tools.name: Get Account Settings
tools.description: Retrieve Zendesk account settings. Use this action when you need to view the configuration and feature flags for a Zendesk account, including API settings, branding, ticket preferences, chat configuration, voice settings, and more.

inputs.name: authenticity_token
inputs.about: Legacy CSRF token. Ignored by API.

tools.name: List Active Triggers
tools.description: List a page of active Zendesk ticket triggers, including their conditions, actions, and metadata when returned. Supports pagination, sorting, and category filtering for auditing automation rules.

inputs.name: page

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Cursor-based pagination only. Possible values are 'alphabetical', 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'position'.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page. Maximum is 100 records per page for the active-triggers endpoint.

inputs.name: sort_order

inputs.name: category_id
inputs.about: Filter triggers by category ID

tools.name: Count Activities
tools.description: Count ticket activities in Zendesk. Returns an approximate count of ticket activities. Use when you need to know how many activities exist in the activity stream for reporting or operational purposes.

tools.name: Get Zendesk Organizations
tools.description: Get Zendesk organizations in an organizations array, automatically fetching numbered pages until an empty page is returned. The action accepts no server-side filters; filter results client-side and disambiguate similar names or domains before acting.

tools.name: Get App
tools.description: Get a single Zendesk app by its numeric ID. Use when you have an app ID and need to retrieve the app's details including name, author information, version, installation count, categories, and description.

inputs.name: app_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk app to retrieve.

tools.name: Get App Installation Requirements
tools.description: List all requirements for a Zendesk app installation. Use when you need to check what configuration or parameters are required for a specific installed app to function properly. Requirements may include OAuth settings, parameter configurations, or other setup steps needed by the app. This action is read-only and idempotent.

inputs.name: app_installation_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the app installation to retrieve requirements for. You can find this ID from the app installations list or when working with specific app installations.

tools.name: Get App Location
tools.description: Get details for a specific Zendesk app location by its numeric ID. Returns location properties including visibility settings, orderability, and associated product codes. Use when you have an app_location_id from listing locations or creating apps and need to retrieve detailed location information. Only accessible to admin users.

inputs.name: app_location_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the app location to retrieve. This is the internal location ID returned by Zendesk when listing or creating app locations.

tools.name: List Apps Location Installations
tools.description: List Zendesk app location installations, returning installation objects and an optional location name. This read-only action is intended for admins.

tools.name: Get App Public Key
tools.description: Retrieves the public key for a specific Zendesk app. The response is in JSON Web Key (JWK) format containing RSA key components (modulus n, exponent e). Use this action when you need to verify JWTs issued by a Zendesk app or establish trust for app-based authentication. This is a read-only operation.

inputs.name: app_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk app whose public key you want to retrieve.

tools.name: Get App Public Key PEM
tools.description: Retrieve a specific Zendesk app's public key in PEM format. This read-only action can be used to verify app-issued JWTs or establish trust for app-based authentication.

inputs.name: app_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk app whose public key in PEM format you want to retrieve.

tools.name: Get Article
tools.description: Retrieve one nonlocalized Zendesk Help Center article by ID.

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: Comma-separated related resources to sideload. Supported values are users, sections, categories, and translations.

inputs.name: article_id
inputs.about: Help Center article ID, as a string.

tools.name: Get Article Attachment
tools.description: Retrieve metadata and the content URL for one article attachment.

inputs.name: article_attachment_id
inputs.about: Unique ID of the Help Center article attachment.

tools.name: Get Article Translation
tools.description: Retrieve one Help Center article translation by article ID and locale.
