tools.name: List User Sessions
tools.description: List all sessions for a specific Zendesk user. Returns details about each active session including authentication time and last seen time. Use this action to monitor session activity for a specific user, investigate security events, or audit login history for account troubleshooting. Use when you need to see all active sessions for a particular user, track their login activity, or investigate potential unauthorized access.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order. Example: `?sort=created_at` or `?sort=-created_at`

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose sessions to retrieve

inputs.name: page_size
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page (max 100).

inputs.name: page_after
inputs.about: Cursor token to fetch records after this position.

inputs.name: page_before
inputs.about: Cursor token to fetch records before this position.

tools.name: Get User's Followed Tickets
tools.description: List tickets the specified Zendesk user is following. Returns all tickets where the specified user is a follower. Use when you need to retrieve all tickets a particular user is watching or tracking, such as for notification purposes, audit trails, or understanding which tickets a user has interest in. Pagination is available for large result sets; follow next_page links until null to retrieve all followed tickets.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: traditional uses '?page=2' (integer page number), cursor uses '?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor' (deepObject with size, after, before). These are mutually exclusive.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Field to sort by: 'id', 'subject', 'deleted_at', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'status', 'requester', 'requester.name', 'group', 'assignee', 'assignee.name'

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose followed tickets to retrieve. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads (assignee_id, requester_id, submitter_id, author_id) or from user listings.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of tickets to return per page (max 100).

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Sort order: 'asc' or 'desc'. Defaults to 'asc'

inputs.name: exclude_archived
inputs.about: If true, excludes archived tickets from the results.

tools.name: List Memberships By User
tools.description: List group memberships for a specific Zendesk user. Use when you need to retrieve all groups a user belongs to, audit user group assignments, or understand which support groups a specific user is a member of. This action is read-only and idempotent. Supports both offset pagination (page, per_page) and cursor pagination (page_size, page_after, page_before). Also supports sideloading users and groups via the include parameter.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number for offset pagination (starts at 1). Cannot be used with cursor pagination.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order. Example: `?sort=group_id` or `?sort=-created_at`

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values. Valid values: `users`, `groups`.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user to retrieve group memberships for. This is the user ID, not a membership ID.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page (max 100).

inputs.name: page_size
inputs.about: Number of records per page for cursor pagination (max 100). Use with page_after. Cannot be used with offset pagination.

inputs.name: page_after
inputs.about: Cursor for fetching next page in cursor pagination. Use with page_size. Cannot be used with offset pagination.

inputs.name: page_before
inputs.about: Cursor for fetching previous page in cursor pagination. Use with page_size. Cannot be used with offset pagination.

tools.name: Get User's Group Membership
tools.description: Get a specific group membership for a user by their IDs. Use when you have both a user ID and a group membership ID and need to retrieve details including the associated group, user, and timestamps. This action retrieves a single group membership record scoped to a specific user, unlike GetGroupMembership which retrieves by membership ID alone, and unlike ListUsersGroupMemberships which lists all memberships for a user.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user. This is the user ID, not a membership ID.

inputs.name: group_membership_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the group membership to retrieve. This is the group membership ID, not a group ID.

tools.name: List User Groups
tools.description: List groups a specific Zendesk user belongs to, with page and per-page parameters, optional exclusion of deleted groups, and sorting. Use it to audit team memberships or retrieve a user's support groups.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: traditional uses `?page=2` (integer page number); cursor uses `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor`. These are mutually exclusive.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order. Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user. Returns groups that this user belongs to.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page. Default and maximum values vary by endpoint.

inputs.name: exclude_deleted
inputs.about: Whether to exclude deleted groups from the response.

inputs.name: include_item_cursors
inputs.about: When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response. Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).

inputs.name: include_boundary_indicators
inputs.about: When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta. Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).

tools.name: Count User Groups
tools.description: Count user groups in Zendesk. Returns an approximate count of groups that a specific user belongs to. Use when you need to know how many groups a user is assigned to for reporting, organizational management, or operational purposes. This action is read-only and idempotent.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose groups to count

tools.name: Show User Identity
tools.description: Tool to show a specific user identity by user ID and identity ID. Use when you need to retrieve detailed information about a particular identity associated with a Zendesk user. This action is read-only and idempotent - it only retrieves data without modifying anything.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user

inputs.name: user_identity_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user identity

tools.name: Get Current Session
tools.description: Retrieve sessions for the currently authenticated Zendesk user, with optional pagination. Session details can include authentication time, last seen time, and user ID.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter for the underlying sessions endpoint. Supports cursor pagination: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size/after/before). Most callers don't need this — current users typically have only a handful of sessions.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of session records to return per page. Maximum is 100 records per page for the sessions endpoint.

tools.name: Get Current User Settings
tools.description: Get the settings for the currently authenticated user in Zendesk. Returns user preferences including Admin Center UI settings, Lotus UI settings (onboarding, tooltips, keyboard shortcuts), and shared views order. Use this action to retrieve the current user's personal settings and preferences.

tools.name: List User Organization Memberships
tools.description: List organization memberships for a specific Zendesk user. Returns membership details including default status, ticket viewing permission, and organization information; the response may contain a next-page URL.

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values. Valid values: 'users', 'organizations'.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose organization memberships to retrieve

tools.name: Get User's Organization Membership
tools.description: Get details for a specific organization membership by user ID and membership ID. Use when you have both a user ID and an organization membership ID and need to retrieve the associated membership metadata including organization details, default status, and ticket viewing permissions. This action is read-only and idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters will return the same result.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user

inputs.name: organization_membership_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the organization membership to retrieve

tools.name: List User Organizations
tools.description: List organizations associated with a specific Zendesk user. Returns a page of organization details, including name, domain names, tags, and custom fields, with pagination options.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: traditional '?page=2' or cursor '?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor'. These are mutually exclusive.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Field to sort results by. Prefix with '-' for descending order. Example: ?sort=name or ?sort=-created_at

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose organizations to retrieve

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page

tools.name: Get User's Organizations Count
tools.description: Returns an approximate count of organizations that a user belongs to. Use when you need to know how many organizations a specific user is associated with in Zendesk.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose organizations to count

tools.name: List User's Organization Subscriptions
tools.description: List User's Organization Subscriptions - retrieves organization subscriptions for a specific user. Use when you need to get all organization subscriptions associated with a particular user, including the organization IDs and creation timestamps. Supports both cursor and offset pagination. End users only see their own subscriptions. This is a read-only operation that does not modify any data.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number for offset pagination (starts at 1)

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose organization subscriptions to list

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of organization subscriptions per page (max 100)

inputs.name: page_size
inputs.about: Number of organization subscriptions per page for cursor pagination (max 100)

inputs.name: page_after
inputs.about: Cursor value to retrieve the next page of results

inputs.name: page_before
inputs.about: Cursor value to retrieve the previous page of results

tools.name: Get User Password Requirements
tools.description: Get password requirements for a specific Zendesk user. Use when you need to retrieve the password policy rules that apply to a user's password, such as minimum length, complexity requirements, or expiration policies. This action is read-only and idempotent.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk user

tools.name: Get Users Profiles
tools.description: Retrieve profiles associated with a specific Zendesk user by user ID. Use when you need to look up user profile information using the Zendesk user ID. This action returns all profiles linked to the specified user account. This action is read-only and idempotent. Note: Access requires agent permissions in Zendesk (Support > People > Roles > People).

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk user whose profiles to retrieve. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads (requester_id, submitter_id, assignee_id, author_id) or from the Users API.

tools.name: Get User Related Info
tools.description: Get related counts and information for a specific Zendesk user by ID. Returns metadata about assigned tickets, CC'd tickets, organization subscriptions, and requested tickets associated with the user. Use when you need to understand the scale and composition of a user's ticket activity and subscriptions in Zendesk. This is a read-only, idempotent operation.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user to retrieve related information for. Must be a non-null integer; cast to int if sourced from tools that return it as a string. Do not pass null (skip the call if user_id is null). Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_USERS, ZENDESK_LIST_USERS, or other user-related actions.

tools.name: Get User's Requested Tickets
tools.description: List tickets requested by a specified Zendesk user, with sorting and offset pagination. The page parameter is limited to pages 1–100.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number for offset pagination (1-100). Limited to first 100 pages or 10,000 records total.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Field to sort by: 'created_at', 'id', 'priority', 'status', 'updated_at'

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose requested tickets to retrieve. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads (requester_id, submitter_id, assignee_id, author_id) or from user listings.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of tickets per page (max 100).

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Sort order: 'asc' or 'desc'

tools.name: List User Requests
tools.description: List ticket requests for a specific Zendesk user. Use when you need to retrieve all requests associated with a particular user ID. This is useful for viewing a user's request history or monitoring their open tickets. This action is read-only and idempotent.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Sort field options for listing user requests.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose requests to retrieve.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Sort order options for listing user requests.

tools.name: List User Skips
tools.description: List ticket skips for a specific user from Zendesk. Use when you need to retrieve all skip records associated with a particular user, such as when analyzing which tickets a user has skipped or reviewing their skip history. This action is read-only and idempotent. Note that archived tickets are not included in the results.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number for offset pagination (starts at 1). Use with per_page to control pagination. Cannot be used with cursor pagination.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk user. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads (requester_id, submitter_id, assignee_id, author_id).

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of skips per page for offset pagination (max 100). Cannot be used with cursor pagination.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Sort order options for listing skips.

tools.name: Get User Tags
tools.description: List all tags assigned to a specific Zendesk user. Use when you need to see what tags are associated with a particular user for organizing, filtering, or categorizing user data. This action is read-only and idempotent.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose tags to retrieve. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads (requester_id, submitter_id, assignee_id, author_id).

tools.name: Count User Assigned Tickets
tools.description: Count tickets assigned to a specific user in Zendesk. Returns an approximate count of tickets where the user is the assignee. Use when you need to know how many tickets are currently assigned to a particular user for workload analysis, reporting, or capacity planning. Note: The count is approximate and may not reflect real-time changes. The count is refreshed periodically rather than being calculated on every request.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose assigned tickets to count. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads (assignee_id, requester_id, submitter_id, author_id).

tools.name: List View Filter Definitions
tools.description: Retrieve Zendesk view filter definitions, including condition, grouping, output, and sorting options available for constructing views.

tools.name: List Views
tools.description: List shared and personal Zendesk views available to the current user, with access, active-status, and group filters. Supports page-number pagination and sorting.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number). Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: The sort parameter used with cursor pagination. Defaults to 'created_at'. Prefix with '-' for descending order.

inputs.name: access
inputs.about: Only views with given access. May be 'personal', 'shared', or 'account'.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Only active views if true, inactive views if false.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: The sort_by parameter used with offset pagination. Possible values are 'alphabetical', 'created_at', or 'updated_at'. Defaults to 'position'.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: Only views belonging to given group.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page. Default and maximum values vary by endpoint.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: The sort_order parameter used with offset pagination. One of 'asc' or 'desc'. Defaults to 'asc' for alphabetical and position sort, 'desc' for all others.

tools.name: List Active Views
tools.description: List all active shared and personal views available in Zendesk. Use when you need to retrieve, audit, or present the view configuration in your Zendesk account. Views define how tickets are filtered, grouped, and displayed to agents. Supports filtering by access type (personal, shared, account), group membership, and sorting preferences.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number for offset pagination. Zendesk returns up to 100 records per page.

inputs.name: access
inputs.about: Possible values for view access type.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Possible values for sorting views.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: Only views belonging to given group

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of views per page for offset pagination (max 100).

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Possible values for sort order direction.

tools.name: List Views - Compact
tools.description: Retrieves a compacted list of shared and personal views available to the current user in Zendesk. Use when you need to quickly fetch a lightweight list of views without full details. This endpoint returns essential view information suitable for dropdown menus or quick selection lists. Unlike the standard /views endpoint, this compact version provides a streamlined response with the most commonly needed fields.

tools.name: Count Views
tools.description: Count shared and personal views in Zendesk. Returns an approximate count of all views (both shared and personal) available in the account. Use when you need to know the total number of views configured for reporting or operational purposes.

tools.name: Count Tickets in Views
tools.description: Count tickets in multiple Zendesk views. Returns the ticket count for each view ID provided in a single API call. Use when you need to quickly get counts for multiple views at once for reporting or dashboard purposes. Note: This is a read-only, idempotent operation. Counts may be cached on the server side.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of view IDs to get counts for (e.g., '1,2,3'). Each ID must be a positive integer. Maximum number of IDs per request is 100.

tools.name: Execute View
tools.description: Execute a Zendesk view to retrieve its column titles and matching ticket rows. Use when you need to run a saved view and get its results - useful for checking which tickets match a view's conditions without manually applying filters. Supports pagination, custom sorting, and optional grouping of results. Returns the view's execution metadata alongside the matching rows.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number). Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.

inputs.name: exclude
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of sideloads to exclude from the response

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of sideloads to include in the response

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: The ticket field used for sorting. This will either be a title or a custom field id.

inputs.name: view_id
inputs.about: The ID of the view to execute

inputs.name: group_by
inputs.about: The ticket field used for grouping. This will either be a title or a custom field id.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: The direction the tickets are sorted. May be one of 'asc' or 'desc'

tools.name: Export View
tools.description: Request an export of a specified Zendesk view and return the response as a downloadable file, along with the view ID and content type.

inputs.name: view_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the view to export. You can find view IDs in the Zendesk admin panel under Views or by listing views via the API.

tools.name: Search Views
tools.description: Search for Zendesk views by their title. Use when you need to find views in your Zendesk account by searching for keywords in their titles. Views are saved searches that display tickets matching specific conditions. This action supports filtering by access level, active status, group, and sorting results.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: traditional uses `?page=2` (integer page number); cursor uses `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). Mutually exclusive.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: Query string used to find all views with matching title. Case-insensitive partial match on view titles.

inputs.name: access
inputs.about: Filter views by access level. Valid values are 'personal', 'shared', or 'account'. When not specified, returns views of all access levels.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Filter views by active status. Set to true to return only active views, or false to return only inactive views. When not specified, returns both active and inactive views.

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: Sideload related data to include in the response. See Zendesk documentation for available sideloads.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Field to sort results by. Options: 'alphabetical' (sorts A-Z), 'created_at' (by creation date), 'updated_at' (by last modification), 'position' (by dashboard position). If unspecified, views are sorted by relevance to the query.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: Filter views by group ID. Only returns views that are assigned to the specified group.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page. Maximum is 100 records per page for the views search endpoint.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Sort order direction. Options: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Defaults to 'asc' for alphabetical and position sorts, 'desc' for created_at and updated_at sorts.

tools.name: List Views By IDs
tools.description: Get multiple Zendesk views by their IDs. Use when you need to retrieve specific views by their IDs in a single request rather than fetching them one by one. The IDs should be provided as a comma-separated string. This action is read-only and idempotent. Returns only views that exist and for which the user has permission.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: List of view IDs separated by commas. Example: '1,2,3'

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Only active views if true, inactive views if false.

tools.name: List Tickets From View
tools.description: List tickets from a specific Zendesk view, with optional sorting and cursor pagination. This read-only action can be used to analyze tickets matching the view's conditions; retrieve additional pages as needed.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Sort or group the tickets by a column in the View columns table. The 'subject' and 'submitter' columns are not supported for sorting.

inputs.name: view_id
inputs.about: The ID of the view to retrieve tickets from

inputs.name: page_size
inputs.about: Number of tickets per page for cursor pagination (max 100). Use cursor-based pagination for large datasets.

inputs.name: page_after
inputs.about: Cursor value to retrieve the next page of results. Obtained from previous response's 'next_page' URL.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Sort order direction. One of 'asc' or 'desc'. Defaults to 'asc' for alphabetical and position sort, 'desc' for all others.

inputs.name: page_before
inputs.about: Cursor value to retrieve the previous page of results. Obtained from previous response's 'previous_page' URL.

tools.name: Count Tickets in View
tools.description: Count tickets in a specific view in Zendesk. Returns the number of tickets matching the view's conditions. Use when you need to know how many tickets are in a particular view for reporting, routing decisions, or workload assessment. The count may be null if the system is still loading and caching new data. This action is read-only and idempotent.

inputs.name: view_id
inputs.about: The ID of the view to count tickets for

tools.name: Get Voice Availability
tools.description: Return one Zendesk Talk agent's availability and current call status.

inputs.name: agent_id
inputs.about: Zendesk user ID of the Talk agent, as a numeric string.

tools.name: List Activities
tools.description: List ticket activities in the last 30 days affecting your Zendesk. Activities include actions like ticket assignments, status changes, comments, and more. This action is read-only and idempotent — use it to monitor ticket activity or build activity feeds.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number). Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). These are mutually exclusive.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order. Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`

inputs.name: since
inputs.about: A UTC time in ISO 8601 format to return ticket activities since said date.

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of sideloads to include. Supported values: `fields_metadata`.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page (max 100).

tools.name: List Custom Roles
tools.description: List all custom roles configured in your Zendesk account. Use when you need to discover available roles, review role configurations, or understand permission structures for your agents. Returns metadata including role names, descriptions, role types, and permission configurations. This is a read-only, idempotent operation with no required parameters.

tools.name: Get Zendesk Organization
tools.description: Get metadata for a specific Zendesk organization by ID. Response fields are available under data.organization_info. Does not return member/user lists.

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: Numeric ID of the organization to retrieve (e.g. 123456). Must be a non-null integer; cast to int if sourced from tools that return it as a string. Do not pass null (skip the call if ticket's organization_id is null). Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS or ZENDESK_CREATE_ZENDESK_ORGANI

tools.name: Get Zendesk Organization Merge
tools.description: Retrieve the details of a specific organization merge operation in Zendesk. This action shows the merge status and the organizations involved. Use when you need to check the status of an organization merge or view details of a past merge operation. This is a read-only, idempotent operation.

inputs.name: organization_merge_id
inputs.about: The ID of the organization merge to retrieve. Must be a non-null string value. This is typically a numeric string ID obtained from a previous organization merge operation.

tools.name: List Organization Subscriptions
tools.description: List organization subscriptions for a specific Zendesk organization, linking users to the organization. This read-only action returns a page of subscriptions with pagination information; page numbers are limited to 100.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number for pagination (1-100). Limited to first 100 pages or 10,000 records total.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of subscriptions per page (max 100).

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: Numeric ID of the organization to retrieve subscriptions for (e.g. 123456). Must be a non-null integer; cast to int if sourced from tools that return it as a string. Do not pass null (skip the call if organization's organization_id is null). Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS or ZENDE

tools.name: List Requests
tools.description: List a page of Zendesk ticket requests, with sorting by creation or update time. This action is read-only and idempotent.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number). Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Sort field options for listing requests.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page. Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific documentation for limits.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Sort order options for listing requests.

tools.name: List Sessions
tools.description: List all active sessions in your Zendesk account. If authenticated as an admin, returns all the active sessions for all users. Otherwise, returns only the sessions for the authenticated user. Use this action to monitor active user sessions, track login activity, or manage session security. Use when you need to audit active user sessions, investigate security events, or retrieve session information for user activity monitoring.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Cursor-based pagination parameters for sessions.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order. When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering. Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`

tools.name: List Sharing Agreements
tools.description: List all sharing agreements for your Zendesk account. Sharing agreements define connections between Zendesk accounts for sharing tickets. This action is read-only and idempotent — use it to view current sharing relationships or check agreement status.

tools.name: List Suspended Tickets
tools.description: List suspended tickets in Zendesk. Suspended tickets are tickets that were automatically held for review due to spam detection, banned content, or other filtering rules. This action is read-only and idempotent — use it to review suspended tickets and determine if they should be recovered or deleted.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number). Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). These are mutually exclusive — use one format or the other, not both.

inputs.name: sort_by

tools.name: List Users
tools.description: Tool to list/enumerate Zendesk users via the Users API. Use when you need to export or iterate through the user directory without a specific name/email filter. Supports both cursor and offset pagination.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number for offset pagination (starts at 1). Cannot be used with cursor pagination.

inputs.name: role

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of users per page for offset pagination (max 100). Cannot be used with cursor pagination.

inputs.name: page_size

inputs.name: role_list
inputs.about: Filter results by multiple roles. Provide a list of roles to include users matching any of them.

inputs.name: page_after
inputs.about: Cursor for fetching next page in cursor pagination. Use with page_size. Cannot be used with offset pagination.

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: Filter by external ID. Must be unique per user under the same account.

inputs.name: permission_set
inputs.about: Filter by custom role ID (Enterprise plan only). Only one role ID per request.

tools.name: Make Zendesk Ticket Comment Private
tools.description: Make a public ticket comment private in Zendesk. This action changes the visibility of a comment from public to internal-only, so only agents can view it. Use this action when you need to convert a customer-facing comment to an internal note after the fact. Note: Only agents can make comments private; end users cannot use this endpoint.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: ID of the ticket containing the comment to make private.

inputs.name: ticket_comment_id
inputs.about: ID of the ticket comment to make private.

tools.name: Make Organization Membership Default
tools.description: Set a specific organization membership as the default for a user in Zendesk. Use when you need to change which organization is the primary/default for a user. Only one organization can be the default at a time. This action is idempotent - setting the same membership as default multiple times will succeed without side effects.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk user whose organization membership you want to set as default. Obtain from ZENDESK_LIST_USERS or ZENDESK_SEARCH_USERS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

inputs.name: organization_membership_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the organization membership to set as the user's default. Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_USERS_ORGANIZATION_MEMBERSHIPS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

tools.name: Make End User Identity Primary
tools.description: Set a specified identity as the primary identity for an end user in Zendesk. This is a collection-level operation - after making an identity primary, you should reload the entire identities collection to get the updated state. An end user can only make an email identity primary if the email is verified. Use when a user wants to change their primary email or phone number for notifications.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the end user

inputs.name: user_identity_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user identity to make primary

tools.name: Make Ticket Comment Private
tools.description: Change a public comment to private on a Zendesk ticket audit. Use when you need to convert a previously public-facing comment to an internal note that is not visible to the end user. This action makes the comment private by updating the ticket audit. This is useful when information was shared publicly by mistake and needs to be restricted to agents only. Note: This action only works on existing audits and cannot be undone once the comment is made private.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket containing the audit.

inputs.name: ticket_audit_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket audit containing the comment to make private.

tools.name: Make User Identity Primary
tools.description: Tool to set a user identity as the primary identity for a Zendesk user. Use when you need to change which email address or identifier is the primary contact method for a user. This action may affect which email notifications the user receives.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user who owns the identity

inputs.name: user_identity_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user identity to make primary

tools.name: Mark Multiple Tickets as Spam
tools.description: Marks multiple tickets as spam in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the tickets will be marked as spam and moved to the suspended tickets queue. The submitter will also be marked as spam and blocked from submitting further tickets. Use when cleaning up spam or unwanted tickets to protect your support queue. Returns a job_status payload for tracking the bulk operation. Note: Tickets marked as spam are moved to the suspended tickets queue and cannot be recovered through normal means.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of ticket IDs to mark as spam. Maximum 100 IDs allowed per request.

tools.name: Merge Users
tools.description: Merges two Zendesk end users together. The user specified in the path parameter (user_id) is the primary user (target) that will be kept. The user specified in the request body (id) is the source user that will be deleted and its data transferred to the primary user. Use when you need to consolidate duplicate end-user accounts in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the source user and all their associated data (tickets, comments, etc.) will be merged into the primary user and the source user cannot be recovered.

inputs.name: user
inputs.about: User object containing the ID of the user to merge from. The 'id' field is mandatory - the source user will be deleted. The 'name' field is optional to rename the primary user.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the primary user (target) to merge another user into

tools.name: Merge Zendesk Tickets
tools.description: Merges multiple tickets into a target ticket in Zendesk. The source tickets are merged into the target ticket and then deleted. This is an asynchronous operation that returns a job status. Use when you need to consolidate duplicate or related tickets into a single ticket. **Important**: This action is irreversible - source tickets are permanently merged and deleted once the operation completes. Always verify the target_ticket_id and source_ticket_ids before executing.

inputs.name: source_comment
inputs.about: Private comment to add to the source tickets before they are merged.

inputs.name: target_comment
inputs.about: Private comment to add to the target ticket after the merge.

inputs.name: target_ticket_id
inputs.about: The ID of the target ticket to merge other tickets into. This ticket will be retained after the merge.

inputs.name: source_ticket_ids
inputs.about: Array of ticket IDs to merge into the target ticket. These tickets will be merged and then deleted.

inputs.name: source_comment_is_public
inputs.about: Whether the comment added to source tickets is public or private. Defaults to false (private).

inputs.name: target_comment_is_public
inputs.about: Whether the comment added to the target ticket is public or private. Defaults to false (private).

tools.name: Open User's Profile in Agent Browser
tools.description: Open a Zendesk user's profile in a specified agent's browser. Use when an agent needs to view a specific user's profile during an active call or session. This action triggers the Zendesk Talk dashboard to display the user's information in the agent's interface.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk user whose profile should be displayed in the agent's browser. You can find this in the user's profile URL or from user search results.

inputs.name: agent_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk agent whose browser should display the user profile. You can find this in the agent's profile URL or from agent listings.

tools.name: Recover Multiple Suspended Tickets
tools.description: Recover multiple suspended tickets in Zendesk. Use when you need to restore tickets that have been suspended (e.g., auto-replied emails, bounced messages). Takes up to 100 ticket IDs as input and restores them to normal ticket status. This action is irreversible — recovered tickets return to normal processing.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of suspended ticket IDs to recover (max 100). Use the auto-generated numeric IDs.

tools.name: Renew Session
tools.description: Renew the current Zendesk session and obtain a new authenticity token. Use when the current session token is expiring or needs to be refreshed to maintain an active authenticated connection. This action extends the session lifetime without requiring full re-authentication.

tools.name: Reorder Custom Object Fields
tools.description: Reorder Custom Fields of an Object. Updates the display order of custom object fields based on the provided field IDs. Use when you need to change the order of fields displayed in a custom object's record layout. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same field IDs in the same order will produce the same result.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

inputs.name: custom_object_field_ids
inputs.about: An array of custom object field IDs specifying the new order. The order of IDs in the array determines the display order of the fields.

tools.name: Reorder App Location Installations
tools.description: Reorder App Installations For Location. Creates or updates the relevant location installation with a specified installation order. This action requires admin-level access. Use when you need to change the display order of apps in a specific Zendesk location (e.g., nav bar, ticket sidebar).

inputs.name: installations
inputs.about: An array of app installation IDs in the desired order. The order of IDs determines the display order in that location.

inputs.name: location_name
inputs.about: The location name where the installations are located. Common values: 'nav_bar', 'ticket_sidebar', 'user_sidebar', 'organization_sidebar', 'new_ticket_sidebar'.

tools.name: Reorder Organization Fields
tools.description: Reorder Organization Fields. Updates the display order of organization fields based on the provided field IDs. Use when you need to change the order of organization fields displayed in Zendesk. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same field IDs in the same order will produce the same result.

inputs.name: organization_field_ids
inputs.about: An array of organization field IDs specifying the new order. The order of IDs in the array determines the display order of the fields in the organization field list.

tools.name: Reorder Ticket Fields
tools.description: Reorder Ticket Fields. Updates the display order of ticket fields based on the provided field IDs. Use when you need to change the order of standard ticket fields displayed in the ticket form. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same field IDs in the same order will produce the same result. This action requires admin permissions.

inputs.name: ticket_field_ids
inputs.about: An array of ticket field IDs specifying the new display order. The order of IDs in the array determines the order of the fields. Only those provided are assigned to first positions; missing IDs get incremental positions automatically.

tools.name: Reorder Ticket Triggers
tools.description: Reorder Ticket Triggers. Updates the firing order of ticket triggers based on the provided trigger IDs. Use when you need to change the priority or execution order of ticket triggers in your Zendesk account. Important constraints: You must include EVERY ticket trigger ID in your account. Omitting any trigger ID returns 404 Forbidden. Additionally, reordering is not permitted if you have more than one ticket trigger category (returns LimitOneCategory error). This action is idempotent - re-running with the same trigger IDs in the same order will produce the same result.

inputs.name: trigger_ids
inputs.about: An array of ticket trigger IDs in the desired firing order. The order of IDs in the array determines the execution order. You must include every ticket trigger ID in your account - omitting any trigger ID returns 404 Forbidden.

tools.name: Reorder User Fields
tools.description: Reorder User Fields. Updates the display order of custom user fields based on the provided field IDs. Use when you need to change the order of user fields displayed in user profiles or forms. This action requires admin-level access. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same field IDs in the same order will produce the same result.

inputs.name: user_field_ids
inputs.about: An array of user field IDs specifying the new display order. The order of IDs in the array determines the position of each field.

tools.name: Reply to Side Conversation
tools.description: Add a message to an existing Zendesk ticket side conversation.

inputs.name: to
inputs.about: Reply recipients. Each recipient must use exactly one routing type: Zendesk user/email, Slack, support group/agent, or Microsoft Teams.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: The plain-text reply body

inputs.name: subject
inputs.about: Reply subject

inputs.name: html_body
inputs.about: An HTML-formatted version of the reply body

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: The Zendesk ticket ID containing the side conversation

inputs.name: external_ids
inputs.about: External metadata to associate with the reply

inputs.name: attachment_ids
inputs.about: IDs of previously uploaded side-conversation attachments

inputs.name: side_conversation_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the side conversation to reply to

tools.name: Reply to Zendesk Ticket
tools.description: Add a public or private comment to a Zendesk ticket, optionally changing its assignee. Comments are public by default.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: Comment content Must contain only the final reply text — do not include draft reasoning or mixed content.

inputs.name: public
inputs.about: Whether the comment is public or internal Public comments are customer-facing and trigger email notifications to the requester; set to false for internal agent notes to prevent unintended customer visibility.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: ID of the ticket to reply to. Note: Closed tickets cannot be updated.

inputs.name: assignee_id
inputs.about: The ID of the agent to assign the ticket to

tools.name: Request End User Verification
tools.description: Send a verification email to an end user to verify ownership of their email address identity. The end user receives an email with a link to confirm their identity. Use when you need to verify an end user's email address identity in Zendesk, such as when creating new end users or resolving identity verification issues. Note: This action can only be performed by verified end users.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the end user

inputs.name: user_identity_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user identity to verify

tools.name: Request User Create
tools.description: Send a request to create a user in Zendesk. This sends the owner a reminder email to update their user profile information. Use when you want to prompt a user to complete their profile through the request flow rather than creating directly. This action is useful for onboarding flows where you want to collect user information through an email-based request rather than creating the user directly.

inputs.name: user
inputs.about: User object containing attributes for the user request. The `name` field is mandatory. This action sends the owner a reminder email to complete their user profile.

tools.name: Request User Verification
tools.description: Send a verification email to a user to verify ownership of their email address identity. The user receives an email with a link to confirm their identity. Use when you need to verify a user's email address identity in Zendesk, such as when creating new users or resolving identity verification issues. Note: This action sends a verification email to the user's identity address.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user

inputs.name: user_identity_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user identity to verify

tools.name: Restore Multiple Deleted Tickets
tools.description: Restore multiple deleted Zendesk tickets by ID. The returned counts and results reflect only results present in the immediate response; a job response without results yields empty counts and results.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of Zendesk ticket IDs to restore. Example: '1,2,3' to restore tickets with IDs 1, 2, and 3. Maximum 100 tickets per request.

tools.name: Restore Zendesk Ticket
tools.description: Restores a previously deleted ticket in Zendesk. Use when a ticket was accidentally deleted and needs to be recovered. The restored ticket will return to its previous state with all associated data intact. This action is reversible — tickets can be deleted again after restoration if needed.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: ID of the deleted ticket to restore.

tools.name: Search Custom Object Records
tools.description: Search and filter custom object records in Zendesk using text queries and field filters. Returns paginated results with cursor-based navigation. Use when you need to find specific records within a custom object type, apply text searches or structured filters, and navigate through large result sets. This is a read-only operation. This action is useful for discovering records, running filtered queries on custom objects, and implementing paginated browsing through custom object data.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Sorting order for custom object records search.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: Search text-based fields for records matching specific terms. Supports fuzzy search on Text, Multi Line Text, and RegExp fields. Multiple words or numbers can be searched (e.g., 'Tesla Honda 2020' matches records containing any of these terms).

inputs.name: filter
inputs.about: Filter object to narrow down search results based on specific field conditions. Structure depends on the custom object's field definitions.

inputs.name: page_size
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page (max 100).

inputs.name: page_after
inputs.about: Pagination cursor for fetching records after a given point. Use 'meta.after_cursor' from a previous response. Cannot be used with page[before].

inputs.name: page_before
inputs.about: Pagination cursor for fetching records before a given point. Use 'meta.before_cursor' from a previous response. Cannot be used with page[after].

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car', 'test_car'). Use ZENDESK_LIST_ZENDESK_CUSTOM_OBJECTS to discover available custom object keys.

tools.name: Search Help Center Articles
tools.description: Search localized Zendesk Help Center articles by text and filters.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Offset page number, starting at 1.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: Text to match in Help Center articles.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.about: Enabled locale to search, such as 'en-us', or '*' for every locale.

inputs.name: section
inputs.about: One or more comma-separated section IDs.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Sort by creation or update time. Omit to sort by relevance.

inputs.name: brand_id
inputs.about: Brand ID to search, as a string.

inputs.name: category
inputs.about: One or more comma-separated category IDs.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of results to return per page, from 1 to 100.

inputs.name: multibrand
inputs.about: Search all brands when true and brand_id is omitted.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Sort direction. Zendesk defaults to descending when a sort field is used.

inputs.name: label_names
inputs.about: Comma-separated article labels. An article matching any label is returned.

tools.name: Search Object Triggers
tools.description: Search triggers for a specific Zendesk custom object by title, description, or active status, with sorting options.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Cursor-based pagination only. Possible values are 'alphabetical', 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'position'.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: Query string used to find all triggers with matching title

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Filter by active triggers if true or inactive triggers if false

inputs.name: filter
inputs.about: JSON-encoded trigger attribute filters for the search. Example: {"json":{"description":"Close a ticket"}}

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: A sideload to include in the response

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Offset pagination only. Possible values are 'alphabetical', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'usage_1h', 'usage_24h', or 'usage_7d'. Defaults to 'position'

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: One of 'asc' or 'desc'. Defaults to 'asc' for alphabetical and position sort, 'desc' for all others

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object to search triggers for

tools.name: Search Zendesk
tools.description: Tool to search for tickets, users, organizations, and groups in Zendesk using query syntax. Use when you need to find resources across Zendesk using flexible search criteria.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number for offset pagination.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: The search query string. Supports Zendesk query syntax for filtering by type, status, priority, etc. Example: 'type:ticket status:open priority:urgent' or 'assignee:me status:pending'.

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: Sideloads to include in the response, returned as top-level arrays alongside `results`. Zendesk's search endpoint requires nested syntax: `<result_type>(<resource1>,<resource2>)`. Combine multiple result types with commas. Common sideloads: `users`, `groups`, `organizations`. A flat comma list (e.g.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.about: Field to sort results by. Options: 'updated_at', 'created_at', 'priority', 'status', 'ticket_type'. Defaults to sorting by relevance if not specified.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of results per page. Default: 10, max: 100.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Sort order direction. Options: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Defaults to 'desc' if not specified.

tools.name: Search Organizations
tools.description: Search organizations in Zendesk by external ID or name. Returns an array of organizations matching the provided criteria. Use when you need to find specific organizations by their identifier or name. An empty organizations array with count=0 means no matches found. Multiple organizations may share similar names — verify the correct organization via external_id or domain_names before proceeding with operations.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of an organization to search for. Supports exact and partial matching.

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: The external id of an organization to search for. Case-insensitive external identifier for linking to external records.

tools.name: Search Zendesk Users
tools.description: Search for Zendesk users by query or external ID. Supports flexible user search criteria using Zendesk search syntax, including names, email, notes, and phone numbers.

inputs.name: page
inputs.about: Page number for offset-based pagination (non-negative integer).

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: The `query` parameter supports the Zendesk search syntax for more advanced user searches. It can specify a partial or full value of any user property, including name, email address, notes, or phone. Example: `query='jdoe'`. See the [Search API](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/search/).

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of sideloads to include in the response.

inputs.name: per_page
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page. Default and maximum values vary by endpoint.

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: The `external_id` parameter does not support the search syntax. It only accepts exact ID values.

tools.name: Set Default Custom Ticket Status
tools.description: Sets one or more custom ticket statuses as the default for their respective categories. Use this action when you need to specify which custom status should be the default (fallback) status for a given category (open, pending, solved, etc.). This operation is idempotent — running it multiple times with the same IDs will produce the same result. **Allowed for**: Admins only. **Note**: The IDs should be valid custom ticket status IDs that exist in your Zendesk account.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of custom status IDs to set as default for their respective categories. Each custom status will become the default for its status category (e.g., open, pending, solved).

tools.name: Set Group Membership as Default
tools.description: Set a group membership as the default for a specific user in Zendesk. Use when you need to mark a user's group membership as the default, meaning tickets assigned directly to the agent will assume this membership's group. Requires both the user ID and the group membership ID. This action is useful for managing default routing preferences for agents in your Zendesk instance. Note that only one group membership can be the default at a time - setting a new default will automatically unset the previous default.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user. This is the user ID, not a membership ID.

inputs.name: group_membership_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the group membership to set as default. This is the group membership ID, not a group ID.

tools.name: Set Organization as Default for User
tools.description: Set an organization as the default for a user in Zendesk. Use when you need to change which organization is the primary/default for a user by specifying the organization ID directly. Only one organization can be the default at a time. This action is idempotent - setting the same organization as default multiple times will succeed without side effects.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the Zendesk user whose default organization to set. Obtain from ZENDESK_LIST_USERS or ZENDESK_SEARCH_USERS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the organization to set as the user's default. Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ORGANISATIONS or ZENDESK_GET_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATION; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

tools.name: Show Access Rule
tools.description: Show a custom object access rule by its ID. Use when you have a custom_object_key and access_rule_id and need to retrieve the access rule's details including its conditions, title, description, and timestamps. This is a read-only operation that does not modify any data. This action is useful for reviewing access control rules applied to custom objects in Zendesk.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The access rule ID

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object

tools.name: Show Custom Object
tools.description: Get details of a specific Zendesk custom object by its key. Use when you have a custom object key and need to retrieve its metadata including name, description, attachment settings, visibility settings, and creation/update timestamps. This is a read-only, idempotent operation that returns the full custom object definition.

inputs.name: include_ui_path
inputs.about: Include UI path in the response. Set to true to retrieve the direct link to the custom object in the Zendesk UI.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

inputs.name: include_permissions_metadata
inputs.about: Include permission metadata in the response. Set to true to retrieve additional permission information for the custom object.

tools.name: Show Custom Object Record
tools.description: Get details of a specific Zendesk custom object record by its key and record ID. Use when you have a custom object key and record ID and need to retrieve the record's metadata including name, custom fields, timestamps, and photo. This is a read-only, idempotent operation that returns the full custom object record definition. Photo is only available if `allows_photos` is enabled on the custom object.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

inputs.name: custom_object_record_id
inputs.about: The id of a custom object record. This is the unique identifier for a specific record within the custom object.

tools.name: Show Many Job Statuses
tools.description: Show many job statuses by their IDs in Zendesk. Use this action when you have multiple job status IDs from bulk operations (like ticket updates, user merges, or ticket merges) and need to check their status in a single request. Each ID in the comma-separated list will return its corresponding job status object if found. Endpoint: GET /api/v2/job_statuses/show_many

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of job status IDs to retrieve. Each id is a 32-char hex token returned by the original async job submission response.

tools.name: Show Many Tickets
tools.description: Show multiple tickets by their IDs. Use when you need to retrieve specific tickets by their IDs to display ticket details, compare tickets, or bulk fetch ticket information. The `ids` parameter accepts a comma-separated list of ticket IDs (e.g., '35436,35437'). Returns tickets for valid IDs only; non-existent IDs result in an empty tickets array without error.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of ticket IDs to retrieve (e.g., '35436,35437' or '35436,35437,35438'). Maximum 100 IDs per request.

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of sideloads to include. Available sideloads depend on the endpoint (e.g., 'users,groups,organizations').

tools.name: Show Many Users
tools.description: Retrieve multiple Zendesk users by their numeric IDs or external IDs. Use when you have a list of user IDs (from ticket payloads, search results, etc.) and need to fetch full user details for multiple users at once. Accepts up to 100 IDs per request. Provide either `ids` or `external_ids`, not both.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of up to 100 user IDs to retrieve (e.g., '1,2,3'). Provide either ids or external_ids, not both.

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of sideloads to include. Available sideloads: 'roles', 'organizations', 'fields', 'photo'. See Zendesk docs for sideloading details.

inputs.name: external_ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of up to 100 external IDs to retrieve users by. Provide either ids or external_ids, not both.

inputs.name: include_deleted
inputs.about: If true, returns inactive or deleted users in the response.

tools.name: Show Permission Policy
tools.description: Get details of a specific permission policy for a Zendesk custom object by its ID. Use when you have a custom_object_key and permission policy ID and need to retrieve the policy's details including the role name and record operation permissions (create, read, update, delete). This is a read-only, idempotent operation that does not modify any data. This action is useful for reviewing permission policies that control access to custom object records in Zendesk.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The permission policy ID. Use format 'custom-role-{custom_role_id}' for custom roles (e.g., 'custom-role-6678128886399') or 'end-user' for the end user system role.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

tools.name: Show Request
tools.description: Show a single request in Zendesk. Use when you need to retrieve details of a specific request by its ID, including subject, description, status, priority, requester information, and other metadata. This action is read-only and idempotent.

inputs.name: request_id
inputs.about: The ID of the request to retrieve

tools.name: Test Webhook
tools.description: Send a diagnostic webhook request through Zendesk.

inputs.name: payload
inputs.about: Serialized payload Zendesk sends to the destination.

inputs.name: endpoint
inputs.about: Destination HTTPS URL for the test request.

inputs.name: webhook_id
inputs.about: Existing Zendesk webhook ID whose settings should be reused.

inputs.name: http_method
inputs.about: HTTP method Zendesk sends to the destination.

inputs.name: custom_headers
inputs.about: Non-credential headers Zendesk sends with the test request.

inputs.name: request_format
inputs.about: Format of the request data Zendesk sends.

tools.name: Unassign User from Organization
tools.description: Immediately removes a user from an organization in Zendesk. Use when you need to unassign a user from an organization membership. This action is irreversible - the user will no longer be associated with the organization.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: The ID of the organization

tools.name: Update Access Rule
tools.description: Update an existing access rule for a custom object in Zendesk. Access rules control which records of a custom object users can access based on conditions. Use this action when you need to: - Change an access rule's title or description - Modify the conditions that determine when the rule applies - Update access permissions for custom object records This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The access rule ID

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the access rule

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: Conditions object for access rules - defines when the rule applies.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A description of what this access rule does

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of the custom object

tools.name: Update Zendesk App Installation
tools.description: Update an app installation in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify app installation settings such as enabling/disabling the app, restricting access by groups or roles, or updating app-specific settings.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.about: If true, the app installation is enabled. Set to false to disable the app for all users.

inputs.name: settings
inputs.about: Installation settings for the app, formatted as a flat key-value object. These are app-specific configuration values.

inputs.name: settings_objects
inputs.about: Installation settings for the app, formatted as an array of objects. Each object should have a 'key' and 'value' field.

inputs.name: role_restrictions
inputs.about: List of role names (as strings) that are allowed to use the app. If empty or null, all roles can use the app.

inputs.name: group_restrictions
inputs.about: List of group IDs (as strings) that are allowed to use the app. If empty or null, all groups can use the app.

inputs.name: app_installation_id
inputs.about: The ID of the app installation to update.

tools.name: Update Article
tools.description: Update selected metadata on one Help Center article.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Article position in its section.

inputs.name: promoted
inputs.about: Whether the article is promoted.

inputs.name: author_id
inputs.about: New article author ID.

inputs.name: article_id
inputs.about: Help Center article ID, as a string.

inputs.name: section_id
inputs.about: Destination section ID.

inputs.name: label_names
inputs.about: Labels replacing the current set.

inputs.name: content_tag_ids
inputs.about: Content tag IDs replacing the current set.

inputs.name: user_segment_id
inputs.about: Single viewer segment ID; null makes the article public.

inputs.name: user_segment_ids
inputs.about: Viewer segment IDs replacing the current set.

inputs.name: comments_disabled
inputs.about: Whether article comments are disabled.

inputs.name: permission_group_id
inputs.about: Permission group allowed to manage the article.

tools.name: Update Article Translation
tools.description: Update editable content and status fields on an article translation.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: New translation body as HTML.

inputs.name: draft
inputs.about: Whether the translation is a draft.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: New translation title.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.about: Current translation locale as a BCP-47 tag, such as en-us.

inputs.name: outdated
inputs.about: Whether the translation is outdated.

inputs.name: article_id
inputs.about: Help Center article ID, as a string.

inputs.name: new_locale
inputs.about: New enabled locale for the translation; omit to keep its current locale.

tools.name: Update Automation
tools.description: Update an existing automation in Zendesk. Automations are business rules that automatically perform actions on tickets when certain conditions are met. Use this action when you need to: - Change an automation's title, active status, or position - Modify the conditions that trigger the automation - Update the actions the automation performs - Deactivate an automation without deleting it This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The new title/name of the automation. Must be unique among all automations.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the automation is active and will execute. Set to false to deactivate the automation.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: List of actions the automation will perform when triggered. Each action specifies a field to modify and the value to set.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The position of the automation which specifies the order it will be executed. Lower numbers execute first.

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: Conditions object for automation - defines when the automation should execute.

inputs.name: automation_id
inputs.about: The ID of the automation to update. You can find automation IDs from the List Automations action or from the automation URL in Zendesk admin.

tools.name: Update Custom Object
tools.description: Update an existing custom object in Zendesk. Custom objects are user-defined data structures that allow you to store and manage custom data types. Use this action when you need to: - Change a custom object's title, description, or pluralized title - Update visibility settings (include_in_list_view) - Enable or disable attachments and photos for the custom object This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: User-defined display name for the object.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: User-defined description of the object.

inputs.name: allows_photos
inputs.about: If true, photos can be uploaded to the records of the object. If false, new photos cannot be uploaded but existing photos can still be viewed and removed.

inputs.name: title_pluralized
inputs.about: User-defined pluralized version of the object's title.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The unique key identifier of the custom object. This is a path parameter that identifies which custom object to update.

inputs.name: allows_attachments
inputs.about: If true, file attachments can be added to the object's records. If false, new attachments can't be added to the object's records, but existing attachments on records can still be viewed and downloaded.

inputs.name: include_in_list_view
inputs.about: A flag setting the visibility of the object in the agent's list view. If true, all agents and admins have viewing access to the object in the Custom objects record page in the Agent Workspace. If false, only admins have viewing access.

tools.name: Update Custom Object Record
tools.description: Update an existing record for a custom object in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify an existing custom object record. This action updates fields on a custom object record. You can update the name, external_id, and custom_object_fields as needed.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: User-defined display name for the object. If autonumbering is selected for the custom object's name field, the name isn't allowed because it's automatically generated. If uniqueness is enabled, the name must be unique.

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: An id you can use to link custom object records to external data. Set to null to remove.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car')

inputs.name: custom_object_fields
inputs.about: A dictionary of custom field key-value pairs. The available fields are defined in the custom object's field definitions. Keys must match field keys from the custom object definition.

inputs.name: custom_object_record_id
inputs.about: The ID of the custom object record to update

tools.name: Update Custom Ticket Status
tools.description: Update an existing custom ticket status in Zendesk. Custom ticket statuses allow you to define additional statuses beyond the standard statuses (new, open, pending, solved, closed) for your ticket workflow. Use this action when you need to: - Change the labels shown to agents or end users for a custom status - Update the descriptions explaining when to use the status - Activate or deactivate a custom status - Modify how a custom status appears in the ticket interface This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result. Requires admin permissions in Zendesk.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: If true, the custom status is set to active. If false, the custom status is deactivated.

inputs.name: agent_label
inputs.about: The dynamic content placeholder or the label displayed to agents. Maximum length is 48 characters.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: The description of when the user should select this custom ticket status. Shown to agents.

inputs.name: end_user_label
inputs.about: The dynamic content placeholder or the label displayed to end users. Maximum length is 48 characters.

inputs.name: custom_status_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the custom ticket status to update. You can find custom status IDs from the List Custom Ticket Statuses action or from the custom status URL in Zendesk admin.

inputs.name: end_user_description
inputs.about: The description displayed to end users. Shown to customers.

tools.name: Update Deletion Schedule
tools.description: Update an existing deletion schedule in Zendesk. Deletion schedules define automated rules for deleting tickets, users, attachments, or other records based on specified conditions. Use this action when you need to: - Change a deletion schedule's title, description, or active status - Modify the conditions that determine which records are deleted - Pause or reactivate a deletion schedule This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result. Note: The 'object' field cannot be modified after schedule creation.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The new title/name of the deletion schedule.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the deletion schedule is active. Set to false to pause the schedule.

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: Conditions object for deletion schedule - defines criteria for matching records.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: The description of the deletion schedule.

inputs.name: deletion_schedule_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the deletion schedule to update. You can find this ID from the deletion schedule URL in Zendesk admin or from listing deletion schedules.

tools.name: Update Dynamic Content Variant
tools.description: Update a specific Zendesk dynamic content item variant by item and variant ID. Content and locale ID are required; active and default status can also be supplied.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the variant is active and usable

inputs.name: content
inputs.about: The new content for the variant

inputs.name: default
inputs.about: Whether the variant is the default for the item it belongs to

inputs.name: locale_id
inputs.about: An active locale ID for this variant

inputs.name: dynamic_content_item_id
inputs.about: The ID of the dynamic content item containing the variant to update

inputs.name: dynamic_content_variant_id
inputs.about: The ID of the variant to update

tools.name: Update Many Dynamic Content Variants
tools.description: Submit a bulk update of variants for a Zendesk dynamic content item, specifying variant IDs or locale IDs and changes to content or status. The response contains a job status for tracking the operation.

inputs.name: variants
inputs.about: List of variants to update. Each variant must include either an 'id' or 'locale_id', and can optionally include 'content', 'active', and 'default'.

inputs.name: dynamic_content_item_id
inputs.about: The ID of the dynamic content item whose variants you want to update

tools.name: Update Macro
tools.description: Update an existing Zendesk macro by ID. The title and actions are required and sent on every update; description, active status, and access restrictions can also be supplied.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the macro.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the macro should be displayed in the UI. Use false to hide the macro without deleting it.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: List of actions the macro will perform. Each action specifies a field to modify and the value to set.

inputs.name: macro_id
inputs.about: The ID of the macro to update. You can find macro IDs from the List Macros action or from the macro URL in Zendesk admin.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: The description of the macro explaining what it does.

inputs.name: restriction
inputs.about: Who may access the macro. Null when everyone in the account can access it.

tools.name: Update Many Automations
tools.description: Update multiple automations in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update automation settings such as position, active status, or title for multiple automations at once. Note: You might be restricted from updating some default automations. If included in a bulk update, the unrestricted automations will be updated. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: automations
inputs.about: List of automations to update. Each automation must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'position', 'active', and 'title'.

tools.name: Update Many Macros
tools.description: Update multiple macros in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update macro settings such as position or active status for multiple macros at once. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: macros
inputs.about: List of macros to update. Each macro must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'position' and 'active'.

tools.name: Update Many Object Triggers
tools.description: Update the position or active status of multiple Zendesk custom object triggers in a single request.

inputs.name: triggers
inputs.about: List of custom object triggers to update. Each trigger must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'position' and 'active'.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
