inputs.about: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car', 'order'). This is a path parameter that identifies which custom object's triggers to update.

tools.name: Update Many Zendesk Organizations
tools.description: Bulk update multiple Zendesk organizations in a single request. Use when you need to update organization details such as name, notes, details, domain names, or tags for multiple organizations at once. The action is queued as a background job - use the job_status URL to poll for completion. Maximum 100 organizations per request. Note: Agents without permission restrictions can only update 'notes' on organizations.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of organization IDs to update (max 100). Required if external_ids is not provided.

inputs.name: external_ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of external organization IDs to update (max 100). Required if ids is not provided.

inputs.name: organizations
inputs.about: List of organizations to update. Each organization must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'name', 'notes', 'details', 'external_id', 'domain_names', and 'tags'. Agents without permission restrictions can only update 'notes'.

tools.name: Update Many Tickets
tools.description: Update multiple tickets in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update ticket fields such as status, priority, tags, assignee, or group for multiple tickets at once. The API accepts up to 100 ticket objects per request. Changes are processed asynchronously and return a job_status object for tracking progress.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of ticket IDs to update. Can be used as an alternative to passing ticket objects in the body. When provided, tickets matching these IDs will be updated with the values from the ticket objects.

inputs.name: tickets
inputs.about: List of ticket update objects. Each object must include an 'id' field and can optionally include 'status', 'priority', 'tags', 'custom_status_id', 'assignee_id', and 'group_id'. Maximum 100 tickets per request.

tools.name: Update Many Ticket Triggers
tools.description: Update multiple ticket triggers in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update trigger settings such as position, active status, or category for multiple triggers at once. This action allows you to update the order (position) or activate/deactivate multiple triggers efficiently. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: triggers
inputs.about: List of triggers to update. Each trigger must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'active', 'position', and 'category_id'.

tools.name: Update Many Users
tools.description: Bulk update multiple Zendesk users in a single request. Use when you need to apply the same or different updates to up to 100 users at once. Provide either a single `user` object to apply identical changes to all specified users, or an array of `users` objects for individual updates per user. The operation is asynchronous and returns a job_status that you can poll to track completion. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will apply the same updates again.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of Zendesk user IDs to update (max 100). Use this when you have the numeric user IDs. Required if external_ids is not provided.

inputs.name: user
inputs.about: Individual user fields to update for bulk operation.

inputs.name: users
inputs.about: Array of user objects to update each user individually. Use this when you need to apply different updates to different users. The number of user objects should match the number of IDs provided.

inputs.name: external_ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of external user IDs to update (max 100). Use this when you have external IDs assigned to users. Required if ids is not provided.

tools.name: Update Many Views
tools.description: Update multiple views in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update view settings such as position, active status, or title for multiple views at once. Note: You might be restricted from updating some default views. If included in a bulk update, the unrestricted views will be updated. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: views
inputs.about: List of views to update. Each view must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'position', 'active', and 'title'.

tools.name: Update Object Trigger
tools.description: Update an existing custom object trigger in Zendesk. Triggers define automated actions that execute when specific conditions are met on custom object records. Use this action when you need to: - Change a trigger's title or description - Enable or disable a trigger - Modify the conditions that cause the trigger to fire - Update the actions the trigger performs This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the trigger. Required in the trigger object for updates.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the trigger is active. Active triggers will execute when their conditions are met.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: An array of actions the trigger performs when its conditions are met. Each action defines what happens when the trigger fires.

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: An object that describes the circumstances under which the trigger performs its actions. Contains 'all' and/or 'any' arrays of condition objects with 'field', 'operator', and 'value'.

inputs.name: trigger_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the trigger to update. This is a path parameter.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A description of what the trigger does.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The unique key identifier of the custom object that owns the trigger. This is a path parameter.

tools.name: Update Organization Field
tools.description: Update a custom organization field in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify an existing organization field's properties such as title, type, description, options, or other settings. All existing custom_field_options must be included on update — omitted options will be deleted. Returns the updated organization field object.

inputs.name: key
inputs.about: A unique key that identifies this custom field. Must consist of only letters, numbers, and underscores. Cannot be only numbers.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.about: Optional tag for checkbox type fields

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The custom field type. Must be one of: checkbox, date, decimal, dropdown, integer, lookup, multiselect, regexp, text, or textarea

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the custom field

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: If true, this field is available for use. If false, the field is hidden from users.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Ordering of the field relative to other fields. Lower values appear first.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: User-defined description of the field's purpose

inputs.name: relationship_filter
inputs.about: Filter definition for autocomplete in lookup fields.

inputs.name: custom_field_options
inputs.about: Required for dropdown or multiselect types. For updates: all existing options must be included (omitted options will be deleted). Pass null id for new options, include id for existing options.

inputs.name: organization_field_id
inputs.about: The ID of the organization field to update

inputs.name: regexp_for_validation
inputs.about: Regular expression pattern for validating regexp type fields

inputs.name: relationship_target_type
inputs.about: Object type referenced for lookup fields. Can be zen:user, zen:organization, zen:ticket, or zen:custom_object:{key}

tools.name: Add Organization Tags
tools.description: Add organization tags in Zendesk. Use when you need to tag an organization for categorization, filtering, or automation purposes. Tags are appended to the organization's existing tags. This action is idempotent — adding the same tag multiple times will not create duplicates in the organization's tag list.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: An array of tag names to add to the organization. Tags will be appended to the existing tags list.

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: The ID of the organization to add tags to

tools.name: Update Permission Policy
tools.description: Update a Zendesk custom object's permission policy, including record access and exceptions. When any record operation is supplied, the request includes all four operations; omitted operations or omitted allowed settings are sent as allowed, with a null rule ID unless specified.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The permission policy ID. Use 'custom-role-{custom_role_id}' for custom roles or 'end-user' for the end user system role.

inputs.name: records
inputs.about: Permission settings for different record operations.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of the custom object

tools.name: Update Resource Collection
tools.description: Update an existing resource collection in Zendesk. Resource collections are groups of related resources (like triggers, automations, or ticket fields) that can be managed together. Use this action when you need to: - Rename a resource collection - Modify the resources included in a collection - Update the configuration of an existing collection This action is idempotent - re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The new name for the resource collection. Must be unique among all resource collections.

inputs.name: resources
inputs.about: List of resources to include in the collection. Each resource object should include 'type' (e.g., 'triggers', 'ticket_fields') and 'resource_id' or 'identifier'.

inputs.name: resource_collection_id
inputs.about: The ID of the resource collection to update. This is a required path parameter.

tools.name: Update Section
tools.description: Update source-locale fields or metadata on a Help Center section.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Section name in its source locale.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.about: Enabled source locale used in the route, such as en-us.

inputs.name: sorting
inputs.about: Article sorting mode.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Section position.

inputs.name: section_id
inputs.about: Help Center section ID, as a string.

inputs.name: category_id
inputs.about: Destination category ID, as a string.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Section description in its source locale; null clears it.

inputs.name: theme_template
inputs.about: Theme template name.

inputs.name: parent_section_id
inputs.about: Parent section ID on eligible plans; null removes the parent.

tools.name: Update Side Conversation
tools.description: Update a side conversation on a ticket in Zendesk. Use this action to modify the state (open/closed) or subject of an existing side conversation attached to a ticket. Use when you need to: - Close a side conversation that has been resolved - Reopen a closed side conversation - Update the subject line of a side conversation This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: state
inputs.about: The new state of the side conversation. Allowed values: 'open' or 'closed'.

inputs.name: subject
inputs.about: The updated subject of the side conversation.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: The ticket identifier. Must be a valid ticket ID that exists in your Zendesk account.

inputs.name: side_conversation_id
inputs.about: The side conversation identifier (UUID format).

tools.name: Update Support Address
tools.description: Update an existing support address in Zendesk. Support addresses are email addresses that receive customer inquiries and can be configured per brand. Use this action when you need to: - Change the name of a support address - Set or change the default support address for the account - Associate a support address with a different brand Note: You cannot change the email address of an existing support address.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The new name for the support address. This is the display name used to identify the address in Zendesk.

inputs.name: default
inputs.about: Whether to set this address as the account's default support address. Set to true to make it the default, false otherwise.

inputs.name: brand_id
inputs.about: The ID of the brand to associate with this support address. Use this to link the address to a specific brand.

inputs.name: support_address_id
inputs.about: The ID of the support address to update. This is a required path parameter that identifies the specific recipient address.

tools.name: Update Zendesk Target
tools.description: Update an existing target in Zendesk. Targets are endpoints that receive data when triggers fire (e.g., HTTP targets, email targets, webhook targets). Use this action when you need to: - Change a target's title - Activate or deactivate a target - Update target-specific properties This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: data
inputs.about: Additional target data to update. Provide any target-specific fields to modify. This allows updating target-type-specific properties beyond title and active status.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The new title of the target

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the target is active

inputs.name: target_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the target to update

tools.name: Update Ticket Field
tools.description: Update an existing ticket field in Zendesk. Ticket fields define the structure and properties of custom fields on tickets. Use this action when you need to: - Rename a ticket field or update its title - Update the description or agent-only description - Change the field's position in the ticket form - Enable or disable a ticket field - Set visibility and editability for portal and agents - Make fields required for solving tickets or creating requests - Configure validation patterns for regexp fields - Set tags for checkbox fields This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result. Requires admin permissions.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.about: For checkbox fields only. A tag added to tickets when the checkbox field is selected

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the ticket field

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether this field is available

inputs.name: creator
inputs.about: If true, displays the creator_user_id and creator_app_name properties in the response. If the ticket field is created by an app, creator_app_name is the name of the app and creator_user_id is -1. If the ticket field is not created by an app, then creator_app_name is null.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The relative position of the ticket field on a ticket. Note that for accounts with ticket forms, positions are controlled by the different forms

inputs.name: required
inputs.about: If true, agents must enter a value in the field to change the ticket status to solved

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Describes the purpose of the ticket field to users

inputs.name: sub_type_id
inputs.about: For system ticket fields of type priority and status. Defaults to 0. A priority sub type of 1 removes the Low and Urgent options. A status sub type of 1 adds the On-Hold option

inputs.name: agent_can_edit
inputs.about: Whether this field is editable by agents

inputs.name: ticket_field_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket field to update

inputs.name: title_in_portal
inputs.about: The title of the ticket field for end users in Help Center

inputs.name: agent_description
inputs.about: A description of the ticket field that only agents can see

inputs.name: visible_in_portal
inputs.about: Whether this field is visible to end users in Help Center

inputs.name: editable_in_portal
inputs.about: Whether this field is editable by end users in Help Center

inputs.name: required_in_portal
inputs.about: If true, end users must enter a value in the field to create the request

inputs.name: collapsed_for_agents
inputs.about: If true, the field is shown to agents by default. If false, the field is hidden alongside infrequently used fields. Classic interface only

inputs.name: regexp_for_validation
inputs.about: For regexp fields only. The validation pattern for a field value to be deemed valid

tools.name: Update Ticket Form
tools.description: Update selected writable configuration fields on a Zendesk ticket form.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Internal name of the ticket form.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the ticket form is active.

inputs.name: default
inputs.about: Whether this is the account's default ticket form.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Position of the ticket form in the form list.

inputs.name: raw_name
inputs.about: Dynamic content placeholder for the name, or the name itself.

inputs.name: display_name
inputs.about: Name of the ticket form shown to end users.

inputs.name: in_all_brands
inputs.about: Whether the ticket form is available in all brands.

inputs.name: ticket_form_id
inputs.about: ID of the ticket form to update.

inputs.name: agent_conditions
inputs.about: Conditional ticket-field rules for agents. An empty array deletes all agent conditions.

inputs.name: end_user_visible
inputs.about: Whether the ticket form is visible to end users.

inputs.name: raw_display_name
inputs.about: Dynamic content placeholder for the display name, or the display name itself.

inputs.name: ticket_field_ids
inputs.about: Ordered IDs of ticket fields included in the form.

inputs.name: end_user_conditions
inputs.about: Conditional ticket-field rules for end users. An empty array deletes all end-user conditions.

tools.name: Update Zendesk Ticket Tags
tools.description: Update tags on a Zendesk ticket via PUT request to /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/tags. Use when you need to add, replace, or manage tags on an existing ticket. This operation replaces all existing tags with the provided list.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: An array of tag names to set on the ticket. Using this endpoint replaces all existing tags on the ticket with the provided tags.

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket to update tags for.

tools.name: Update Ticket Trigger
tools.description: Update an existing ticket trigger in Zendesk. Triggers are business rules that automatically perform actions on tickets when certain conditions are met. Use this action when you need to: - Change a trigger's title, active status, position, or description - Modify the conditions that trigger the action - Update the actions the trigger performs - Reassign a trigger to a different category - Deactivate a trigger without deleting it This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The new title/name of the trigger. Must be unique among all triggers.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the trigger is active and will execute.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.about: List of actions the trigger will perform when triggered. Each action specifies a field to modify and the value to set.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The position of the trigger which specifies the order it will be executed. Lower numbers execute first.

inputs.name: conditions
inputs.about: Conditions object for trigger - defines when the trigger should execute.

inputs.name: trigger_id
inputs.about: The ID of the trigger to update. You can find trigger IDs from the List Triggers action or from the trigger URL in Zendesk admin.

inputs.name: category_id
inputs.about: The ID of the category to assign the trigger to. Categories help organize triggers in the Zendesk admin interface.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A description of what the trigger does.

tools.name: Update Trigger Category
tools.description: Update an existing trigger category in Zendesk. Trigger categories are used to organize ticket triggers in the Zendesk admin interface. Use this action when you need to: - Rename a trigger category - Change the display order of a trigger category - Update both name and position of a trigger category This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The new name of the trigger category. Must be unique among all trigger categories.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The new position of the trigger category which specifies the order it will be displayed. Lower numbers appear first.

inputs.name: trigger_category_id
inputs.about: The ID of the ticket trigger category to update.

tools.name: Update User
tools.description: Update selected core fields on one Zendesk user by numeric user ID.

inputs.name: user
inputs.about: Core user fields to update. At least one field is required.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: ID of the Zendesk user to update, as a string.

tools.name: Update Zendesk User Field
tools.description: Update an existing user field in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify the title, description, options, or other properties of a custom user field. Supports updating text, checkbox, dropdown, multiselect, date, integer, decimal, regexp validation, and lookup types. Only administrators can update user fields.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.about: Tag value for checkbox fields

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The new title (label) displayed for this custom field

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: If true, this field is available for use

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Ordering of the field relative to other user fields

inputs.name: raw_title
inputs.about: Dynamic content placeholder for title (supports i18n placeholders)

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: New user-defined description of this field's purpose

inputs.name: user_field_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user field to update. This is the field's unique numeric identifier in Zendesk, not the field key.

inputs.name: raw_description
inputs.about: Dynamic content placeholder for description (supports i18n placeholders)

inputs.name: relationship_filter
inputs.about: Filter configuration for relationship-type user fields.

inputs.name: custom_field_options
inputs.about: Updated options for dropdown or multiselect fields. Each option has a name (display) and value (internal tag).

inputs.name: regexp_for_validation
inputs.about: Regular expression pattern for validating field values

inputs.name: relationship_target_type
inputs.about: Target type for 'lookup' fields. Options: 'zen:user', 'zen:organization', 'zen:ticket', 'zen:custom_object:{key}'

tools.name: Update Zendesk User Profile
tools.description: Partially updates a user profile in Zendesk by identifier. Use when you need to modify specific fields of an existing profile without replacing the entire profile. This action uses JSON merge patch semantics — only provided fields are updated. Use this action when you have an existing profile identifier and need to update specific profile attributes, identifiers, or the profile name. The identifier must follow the format source:type:identifier_type:identifier_value.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Person's name to set on the profile

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: Profile type (e.g., 'contact', 'user', 'account')

inputs.name: source
inputs.about: Source application/system for the profile (e.g., 'company'). Cannot be 'zendesk' as it is reserved.

inputs.name: attributes
inputs.about: JSON schema compliant object containing profile attributes/details

inputs.name: identifier
inputs.about: Profile identifier in format source:type:identifier_type:identifier_value (e.g., company:contact:email:john@example.com). All identifiers must belong to a single user and profile.

inputs.name: identifiers
inputs.about: List of identifiers for the profile. Each identifier must have a type and value.

tools.name: Update Zendesk User Profile By ID
tools.description: Partially updates a user profile in Zendesk by profile ID. Use when you need to modify specific fields of an existing profile without replacing the entire profile. This action uses JSON merge patch semantics — only provided fields are updated. Use this action when you have a profile ID and need to update specific profile attributes, identifiers, name, source, or type. This is different from UpdateUserProfile which uses identifier lookup instead.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Person's name to set on the profile

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: Profile type (e.g., 'contact', 'user', 'account')

inputs.name: source
inputs.about: Source application/system for the profile (e.g., 'company'). Cannot be 'zendesk' as it is reserved.

inputs.name: attributes
inputs.about: JSON schema compliant object containing profile attributes/details

inputs.name: profile_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the Sunshine profile to update. This is the profile ID returned when the profile was created.

inputs.name: identifiers
inputs.about: List of identifiers for the profile. Each identifier must have a type and value.

tools.name: Update User Identity
tools.description: Update the verified status of a specific Zendesk user identity by user ID and identity ID.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user who owns the identity

inputs.name: verified
inputs.about: If true, marks the identity as verified. Deprecated - use verification_method instead for more accurate verification states.

inputs.name: user_identity_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user identity to update

tools.name: Update Current User Settings
tools.description: Update the settings for the currently authenticated Zendesk user. Use when modifying UI preferences like keyboard shortcuts, onboarding tooltips, theme preferences, or shared views order. This action modifies the caller's own settings only.

inputs.name: settings
inputs.about: User settings to update. Can include lotus, admin_center, and shared_views_order.

tools.name: Update Users Profiles
tools.description: Create or update a profile for a specified Zendesk user, identified by user ID and a profile lookup identifier. Supply the profile's name and identifiers, with optional custom attributes, to establish or modify the user's profile.

inputs.name: profile
inputs.about: Profile object containing the profile data with name, identifiers, and optional attributes

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The Zendesk user ID (numeric string) of the user to associate with the profile

inputs.name: identifier
inputs.about: Profile lookup identifier in format 'source:type:identifier_type:identifier_value' (e.g., 'company:contact:email:user@example.com'). This identifies which profile to create or update for the specified user.

tools.name: Update User Tags
tools.description: Update (replace) tags for a specific Zendesk user. Use when you need to assign or modify tags on a user account for organizing, filtering, or categorizing user data. This action replaces all existing tags on the user with the provided list.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: An array of tag strings to assign to the user. This will replace all existing tags on the user with the provided list. Tags are used to categorize and organize users.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user whose tags to update. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads or user search results.

tools.name: Update View
tools.description: Update an existing Zendesk view's title, description, active status, position, or default status. Views are saved ticket filters used to organize agent workflows.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the view

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the view is active

inputs.name: default
inputs.about: If true, the view is a default view

inputs.name: view_id
inputs.about: The ID of the view to update

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: The position of the view in the list

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: The description of the view

tools.name: Update Zendesk Account Settings
tools.description: Update Zendesk account-level settings including tickets, branding, localization, routing, and more. Use when you need to configure or modify account-wide settings that affect all agents and end users. Requires admin privileges to update most settings. Settings changes are persistent and affect all users.

inputs.name: settings
inputs.about: The account settings to update. Must include at least one setting category.

tools.name: Update Zendesk Attachment
tools.description: Updates an attachment's malware access override setting. Use when you need to enable or restrict agent access to attachments that have been flagged for malware.

inputs.name: attachment_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the attachment to update

inputs.name: malware_access_override
inputs.about: If true, allows agents to access attachments with detected malware. If false, restricts access to malware-detected attachments.

tools.name: Update Custom Object Field
tools.description: Update an existing custom object field in Zendesk. Custom object fields define the structure and properties of data within a custom object. Use this action when you need to: - Rename a custom object field - Update the description or display properties - Change the field's position in the UI - Enable or disable a field - Set validation patterns or make fields required This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: User-defined display name for the field.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: If true, the field is active and can be used. If false, the field is inactive and hidden in the UI.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Position of the field in the UI. Lower values are displayed first.

inputs.name: required
inputs.about: If true, the field is required when creating or updating records. If false, the field is optional.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: User-defined description of the field.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car'). This is a path parameter that identifies the parent custom object.

inputs.name: regexp_for_validation
inputs.about: A regular expression pattern used to validate the field value. Only applies to text-type fields.

inputs.name: custom_object_field_key_or_id
inputs.about: The key or id of a custom object field. This can be either the human-readable key (e.g., 'make') or the numeric ID of the field.

tools.name: Update Dynamic Content Item
tools.description: Update a dynamic content item in Zendesk. The only attribute that can be changed is the name. Use when you need to rename an existing dynamic content item after confirming its ID. Note: Dynamic content items are used to store multilingual content for use in triggers, automations, and macros. Updating the name affects all references to this item.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The new name for the dynamic content item. The name must be unique and is used as the identifier when referencing this item in triggers, automations, or dynamic content templates.

inputs.name: dynamic_content_item_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the dynamic content item to update. You can get this ID from the item's URL or by listing dynamic content items.

tools.name: Update Zendesk Organization
tools.description: Update an organization in Zendesk. After updating, re-fetch via ZENDESK_GET_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATION if downstream logic depends on current data.

inputs.name: data
inputs.about: New data for the organization Must use valid Zendesk organization field names (e.g., `name`, `notes`, `domain_names`, `external_id`); invalid fields may be silently ignored. `domain_names` must be an array and is treated as a full replacement — always include existing domains alongside new ones to a

inputs.name: organization_id
inputs.about: ID of the organization to update Verify the exact ID before updating — multiple organizations may share similar names and updates are persistent.

tools.name: Update Request
tools.description: Update a Zendesk ticket request by ID, including fields such as status, priority, assignment, tags, and custom fields, or add a comment.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: Tags to set on the request. Using this replaces all existing tags.

inputs.name: solved
inputs.about: Whether or not the request is solved. An end user can set this if 'can_be_solved_by_me' is true for that user.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: The state of the request after the update. Allowed values: 'new', 'open', 'pending', 'hold', 'solved', 'closed'.

inputs.name: comment
inputs.about: Comment object for adding a comment to the request.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: The ID of the group to assign the request to.

inputs.name: priority
inputs.about: The priority of the request. Allowed values: 'urgent', 'high', 'normal', 'low'.

inputs.name: request_id
inputs.about: The ID of the request to update. Find this ID from the request URL or from a list requests action.

inputs.name: assignee_id
inputs.about: The ID of the agent to assign the request to. The agent must be a member of the group the request is assigned to.

inputs.name: custom_fields
inputs.about: Custom field values to set on the request. Each item should include 'id' (field ID) and 'value'.

tools.name: Update Zendesk Ticket
tools.description: Tool to update a ticket in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify ticket fields like status, priority, or subject after confirming the ticket ID.

inputs.name: data
inputs.about: Optional raw ticket update object. Provide this to send fields under the 'ticket' wrapper directly. Alternatively, use the un-nested fields above.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: Tags to set on the ticket. Using tags here replaces all existing tags.

inputs.name: due_at
inputs.about: Due date/time for task-type tickets (ISO 8601).

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Ticket status category. Allowed values: new, open, pending, hold, solved. Note: If your account has custom statuses enabled, use custom_status_id instead.

inputs.name: subject
inputs.about: Ticket subject/title to set during update.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the group to assign the ticket to.

inputs.name: metadata
inputs.about: Custom metadata to attach to this update's audit (approximately up to 1 KB).

inputs.name: priority
inputs.about: Ticket priority. Allowed values: urgent, high, normal, low. Values are case-sensitive.

inputs.name: email_ccs
inputs.about: Email CCs to add/remove. Each object includes user_id or user_email, optional user_name, and action ('put'|'delete').

inputs.name: followers
inputs.about: Followers to add/remove. Each object should include user_id or user_email, with optional action ('put'|'delete').

inputs.name: ticket_id
inputs.about: ID of the ticket to update.

inputs.name: assignee_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the agent to assign the ticket to. The agent must be a member of the group the ticket is assigned to. Use this parameter directly rather than passing through data to avoid 400 errors.

inputs.name: safe_update
inputs.about: Enable optimistic locking to prevent overwrites during collisions. Must be paired with updated_stamp to take effect.

inputs.name: comment_body
inputs.about: Text body of the comment to add.

inputs.name: collaborators
inputs.about: Collaborators to set (replaces existing). Accepts user IDs, emails, or {name, email} objects.

inputs.name: custom_fields
inputs.about: List of custom field values. Each item: {id: number, value: any}.

inputs.name: updated_stamp
inputs.about: Last-known updated_at timestamp (ISO 8601) used together with safe_update.

inputs.name: comment_public
inputs.about: Whether the added comment is public (visible to requester) or internal. Defaults to true (public); set false to create an internal note.

inputs.name: comment_uploads
inputs.about: Upload tokens to attach files to the comment.

inputs.name: collaborator_ids
inputs.about: Collaborator user IDs to set (replaces existing).

inputs.name: custom_status_id
inputs.about: The ID of a custom ticket status. Required for accounts with custom statuses enabled. Use this instead of 'status' when custom statuses are active. Retrieve available custom status IDs from the Custom Ticket Statuses API.

inputs.name: comment_author_id
inputs.about: Author ID for the comment, if different from the authenticated user.

inputs.name: comment_html_body
inputs.about: HTML body of the comment to add.

inputs.name: additional_collaborators
inputs.about: Add collaborators without removing existing ones.

tools.name: Upsert Custom Object Record By External ID or Name
tools.description: Create or update a Zendesk custom object record by external ID or name, with external ID taking precedence when both are supplied. If no name is supplied in the request or record data, the payload uses “Untitled Record” as the name.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of a custom object record. If a record with this name exists (and no external_id matches), it will be updated. If no record is found and external_id is provided, a new record will be created.

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: The external id of a custom object record. If a record with this external_id exists, it will be updated. If not found and name is provided, a new record will be created with this external_id.

inputs.name: record_data
inputs.about: Schema for a custom object record.

inputs.name: custom_object_key
inputs.about: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

tools.name: Verify Subdomain Availability
tools.description: Verify if a subdomain name is available for use in Zendesk. Returns a success boolean indicating whether the subdomain can be registered. Use when checking if a desired subdomain name is available before creating a new Zendesk account or subdomain.

inputs.name: subdomain
inputs.about: The subdomain name to verify. The name cannot contain underscores, hyphens, or spaces.

tools.name: Verify Support Address
tools.description: Verify a support address forwarding in Zendesk. This action sends a verification request for the specified support address to confirm that the address is properly configured and can receive email forwarding. Use this action when you need to: - Verify a newly created support address is working correctly - Re-verify an existing support address after configuration changes - Confirm email forwarding is properly set up for a support address This action is idempotent — verifying an already-verified address will return success.

inputs.name: support_address_id
inputs.about: The ID of the support address to verify. You can find this ID from the support address listing or from the address details in Zendesk admin.

tools.name: Verify User Identity
tools.description: Set a user identity as verified in Zendesk. This action marks an email address or other identity as confirmed, indicating the user has proven ownership. Use when you need to manually verify a user's identity after they have completed an out-of-band verification process or when you want to override the verification status for administrative purposes. Note: This action cannot verify the account owner's email identity due to security restrictions.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user

inputs.name: user_identity_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the user identity to verify
